requirement: generateToolTipFragment(String toolTipText) throws IllegalArgumentException (via the delegate htmlEscape call) when toolTipText is null, rather than producing a fragment containing the literal text 'null'.

When the cached bounds are recomputed over all cells, the minimum range bound equals the smallest min-outlier value attained by any stored item and the maximum range bound equals the largest max-outlier value attained by any stored item; stored items whose minOutlier or maxOutlier is null or whose corresponding value is NaN contribute nothing to that extreme (their NaN must not corrupt the cached bounds).

getDataRange(ValueAxis) iterates over each non-null dataset mapped to the queried axis; when such a dataset has no renderer (getRendererForDataset returns null), the method must not throw a NullPointerException from accessing that renderer's annotations — instead it simply continues (no renderer-supplied annotations from that dataset are scanned/collected), and the computed range is derived only from the available data bounds.

When PosixParser flatten/parse runs in stop-at-non-option mode (stopAtNonOption=true) and it encounters a plain argument token (one that does not start with '-') immediately after a recognized option that takes an argument, that token is NOT treated as the stopping point: PosixParser does not insert the '--' separator before it and does not gobble the remaining tokens; instead the token is emitted as a separate plain token so that it is consumed as that option's argument value (in parsing terms the option's value equals that token and remaining option syntax is still parsed).

When a text to be rendered (wrapped) over multiple lines requests a continuation indent nextLineTabStop that is greater than or equal to the total line width, the wrapping process always terminates and produces the full wrapped output, instead of entering the previously unbounded re-wrapping loop that hung indefinitely for inputs such as an option with a run-on description rendered under a narrow total width.

When, after parsing, there is exactly one missing required option, the thrown MissingOptionException's message equals 'Missing required option: ' followed by the missing option's key (and is not just the bare key).

ReferenceCollection.isAssignedOnceInLifetime now returns false (previously true) when, walking outward from the variable's sole assignment reference, a function basic-block is reached before any loop and that function's scope differs from the scope of the variable's declaring symbol; i.e. an assignment placed inside an inner/nested function scope capturing the variable is treated like an assignment that can execute more than once, not as an assignment occurring exactly once in the variable's lifetime, even though only one assignment statement exists and no enclosing loop is present.

When transforming a BLOCK_COMMENT, IRFactory reports the SUSPICIOUS_COMMENT_WARNING (at the comment's line) if the comment text contains an '@'-annotation whose '@' immediately follows a '*' that itself follows a '/' (i.e., the comment opener), allowing any run of zero or more space/tab characters between the '*' and the '@' — covering compact '/*@name' as well as '/* @name' / '/*\t@name' forms.

When a ternary conditional (?:) expression appears directly in a for(...) init-clause, any `in` operator occurring inside its consequent (true) or alternate (false) operand is printed parenthesized, so the emitted code re-parses to the same ternary AST rather than the `in` being interpreted bare (e.g. as a for-in clause or a top-level relational in that context); ternaries not inside a for-init clause are printed exactly as before (branches in OTHER context).

When TypeCheck visits a `new X(...)` expression whose constructor's type, after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined, is classified as a constructor/empty/unknown type AND resolves to a non-null FunctionType that reports no instance type (fnType.hasInstanceType() == false), TypeCheck does not proceed down the normal-constructor path; instead it falls into the fallback that leaves the NEW node typed only via ensureTyped (i.e. it does not dereference/getInstanceType of that FunctionType or validate the argument list against its parameters).

When an unconditional control-flow jump — an argument-less return, a break, or a continue — is otherwise eligible for removal (its single branch target equals its computed fall-through/follow node, so that removing it would preserve control flow), UnreachableCodeElimination must NOT remove it if that jump statement is lexically contained within the body of the finally clause of any enclosing try statement. The jump is preserved in the (nominally unchanged) output regardless of how deeply it is nested inside the finally body, including within nested (multi-level) finally blocks.

When the retraversal pass iterates over the children of a node, a child's subtree optimization (which may structurally mutate the tree, detaching or rewriting nodes) must not affect which sibling is processed next: the caller's iteration continues from the sibling that followed the child before the child was traversed, so no original sibling is skipped or revisited and the loop makes forward progress to a fixed point.

CollapseProperties.inlineAliases does not treat a global qualified name declared in the externs (name.inExterns == true) as an alias-inlining candidate, even when it otherwise satisfies condition (b) (exactly one global set, no local sets, more than zero aliasing gets); consequently CollapseProperties leaves local aliases/references that read or alias such extern-declared names unmodified (not inlined, not rewritten to flattened names, not nulled out).

InlineRenamer registers a hard invariant that it is never asked to add "arguments" as a declared name: InlineRenamer.addDeclaredName("arguments") throws an IllegalStateException rather than planning any rename for the special arguments binding.

Compiler.toSource resolves the code-generation charset from the output charset option by name (Charset.forName) whenever that option is set, and uses no charset (ASCII/escaping mode) when the option is unset; consequently, when an output charset that can represent a character (e.g. UTF-8 with non-Latin1 characters) is in effect, that character is emitted literally rather than as a \uXXXX unicode escape.

The FlowSensitiveInlineVariables pass treats a property-deletion expression (`delete <expr>`, a DELPROP node) as a side-effecting operation for its inlining side-effect analysis, and consequently does NOT perform flow-sensitive inlining of a variable when such a `delete` expression occurs where the pass checks for side effects (in the sub-expressions on the right of the variable's def, in the sub-expressions on the left of the variable's use, or on the CFG path between a non-adjacent def and use); such candidate variables are left unmodified rather than replaced by their definition's value.

When CompilerOptions.checkSymbols is false but the warning guards already installed on the supplied CompilerOptions (options.getWarningsGuard as populated, e.g. via setWarningLevel(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_VARIABLES, ...)/addWarningsGuard called before init) enable the CHECK_VARIABLES diagnostic group, Compiler.initOptions does NOT append a CHECK_VARIABLES-OFF suppression guard, so undefined-variable (VarCheck.UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR) and multiply-declared-variable (SyntacticScopeCreator.VAR_MULTIPLY_DECLARED_ERROR) diagnostics emitted by the variable-check pass are reported at the level configured by the user rather than being silenced.

When a variable is declared with an explicitly declared (non-inferred) type and its initializer expression's inferred type is the void/undefined type, the in-flow type of that variable after the declaration statement is the void/undefined type (not the declared type), so subsequent uses in that scope are type-checked against undefined rather than against the declared type.

During source setup (parseInputs), dependency management runs whenever options.dependencyOptions.needsManagement() is true, regardless of whether options.closurePass is enabled: each input's provided types are forward-declared in the type registry and inputs are re-sorted so that they satisfy their required/provided reordering.

In an array-literal .join(...) call whose sole argument is the string literal ',' (equal to the join default separator), that redundant ',' argument is removed from the call (reporting a code change) before folding proceeds, so the call is folded/simplified as though no explicit separator had been passed.

For an expression-statement call whose callee is a GETPROP with qualified name exactly 'goog.provide', extractClassNameIfProvide extracts (returns) the class name only when the call's first argument node is a STRING literal; if the argument is a non-null node that is not a STRING token (e.g. a variable reference, a GETPROP/qualified name, or a non-null child of some other token type), it returns null instead of extracting anything from that argument.

NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects returns false (no side effects) for a CALL node whose callee is a GETPROP whose object is a single NAME whose string equals "Math" (i.e. a direct call of the form Math.<member>(...)), regardless of whether a compiler is supplied and regardless of the hasRegExpGlobalReferences condition.

Restricting an object type on the knowledge that its typeof result equals "function" (true condition) narrows the type to its callable/constructable sub-region (the greatest subtype of the object type within the function/constructor types): an object type that is itself already a function value is preserved as that function (non-null) rather than eliminated just because it does not wholly contain the generic constructor type, and a broad object supertype narrows to the generic function/constructor type.

NodeUtil.isStrWhiteSpaceChar returns TernaryValue.UNKNOWN (no longer TernaryValue.TRUE) for the vertical-tab character (\u000B / VT), i.e. VT is no longer classified as definitively trimmable whitespace.

When an assignment (including compound assignments such as += and -=) is transformed whose left-hand/target operand is not a valid lvalue (a node whose type is not one of NAME, GETPROP, or GETELEM), IRFactory reports an error with message "invalid assignment target", reported at the target node's line number.

Dead assignment elimination no longer treats an assignment `v = RHS` (to a local variable `v`) as an unconditional kill of `v` when the assignment lies to the right of another value-producing assignment to `v` within the same expression: if `RHS`'s first reference to `v` is a read (a read occurring before any write to `v` within `RHS`), the live-ness scan reports a READ for that assignment instead of a KILL, so the earlier assignment to `v` is preserved (not eliminated) because its value is observable through that RHS read. Observable case: `if ((a=1)&&(b=a))` keeps `a=1`, and `return (x=1) && (x=f(x))` keeps `x=1`.

When ProcessCommonJSModules computes the module name for a script node in visitScript, it passes the raw source file name to guessCJSModuleName, which performs the (single) prefix-strip normalization internally; the earlier redundant outer normalizeSourceName call is gone. Because normalizeSourceName removes the configured filename prefix only once, a file whose path contains the configured prefix text again after the leading occurrence now keeps that later occurrence (and the filename prefix is stripped exactly once rather than twice), affecting the resulting module identifier.

isValidDefineValue recognizes expressions built from the binary operators + (ADD), - (SUB), * (MUL), / (DIV), % (MOD), < (LT), <= (LE), > (GT), >= (GE), == (EQ), != (NE), === (SHEQ), !== (SHNE), << (LSH), >> (RSH), >>> (URSH) as valid define values when both operands are themselves valid define values; previously none of these operator nodes was recognized and they all evaluated to false/invalid.

ReferenceCollection.isAssignedOnceInLifetime() returns false when the variable has exactly one assignment (single l-value or initializing declaration as computed by getOneAndOnlyAssignment) but that sole assignment occurs inside a loop body (DO, WHILE, or FOR) within the function scope containing the assignment.

A MultiValueMap instance is an instanceof java.io.Serializable (the class now implements Serializable and declares a serialVersionUID), so mapping it to a plain serialization operation is no longer rejected for the map's own lack of serializability.

SetUniqueList.subList(int fromIndex, int toIndex) returns an unmodifiable list: any mutating operation attempted on the returned view (such as via List.add/set/remove or its list iterator's add/remove/set) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so structural changes cannot be made through the subList to invalidate the parent list.

Calling close() while the current entry's written byte count does not equal the entry's declared size (e.g. an entry left partially/unwritten) now throws an IOException describing the invalid entry size, rather than silently closing the underlying stream.

Rebuilding ZipFile's entry-to-offset table during resolveLocalFileHeaderData re-registers every entry (with its OffsetEntry) in the same central-directory enumeration order regardless of whether that entry's name was changed to its Unicode form, so that no entry is lost, dropped, or reordered out of central-directory order by the reconstruction.

When ZipArchiveEntry.setName is invoked on an entry whose platform is PLATFORM_FAT with a non-null name that contains no forward-slash '/', the stored name (as later returned by getName) has every backslash '\' character replaced by '/'.

When serializing a bitset whose length (number of entries) is a positive multiple of 8 — i.e. the bits exactly fill whole 8-bit groups — SevenZOutputFile's bit serialization writes exactly length/8 bytes and does not emit an extra trailing byte for the final, already-full byte group.

TarUtils.parseOctal throws IllegalArgumentException when an octal field contains no octal-digit content at all (i.e., after skipping leading spaces and trimming trailing NULs/spaces nothing remains); in particular a field consisting solely of space bytes now throws IllegalArgumentException rather than returning 0.

When reading data from the current tar entry, if the underlying input stream signals EOF by returning -1 while the requested read length (numToRead, already capped by the current entry's remaining available bytes) is greater than 0, then read(byte[],int,int) throws an IOException whose message is "Truncated TAR archive", rather than silently recording end-of-archive.

DeflateCompressorInputStream.matches(byte[] signature, int length) returns false when length <= 3; otherwise it returns true exactly when signature[0] equals byte 0x78 and signature[1] equals (byte) 0x01, 0x5e, 0x9c, or 0xda, and false otherwise.

When TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders scans a PAX header for the decimal length of a record, a newline ('\n') byte encountered where length digits would otherwise be accumulated is treated as a blank/stray line that is skipped without contributing to the parsed length; parsing then resumes at the start of the next record, so that all valid `length keyword=value\n` records still populate the returned Map even when blank lines intervene in the header stream (instead of the newline being folded into the length, which yields a corrupt/negative length and garbled results).

CpioArchiveOutputStream.close() closes the underlying (filtered) output stream and marks the stream as closed but does not write the CPIO trailing trailer entry; an archive that is closed without having previously called finish() is left unterminated, i.e. its produced bytes contain no CPIO trailer record.

ZipArchiveInputStream.canReadEntryData returns false for a ZipArchiveEntry whose compressed size is ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN, unless the entry's compression method tolerates an unknown size, i.e. it is DEFLATED, ENHANCED_DEFLATED, or STORED fired only when the entry uses a data descriptor and allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is enabled (all other methods with an unknown compressed size now yield false).

TarArchiveOutputStream.getCount() (deprecated override) returns the wrapped CountingOutputStream's byte count truncated to an int, i.e. returns (int) getBytesWritten() rather than the value of the base-class ArchiveOutputStream bytesWritten field.

For a Map type whose raw class is assignable to java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentMap but NOT to java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentNavigableMap (e.g., the ConcurrentMap interface), the ObjectConstructor's construct() returns a java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap instance.

JsonReader.nextLong() no longer throws IllegalStateException when the current token is an unquoted literal (peek state PEEKED_UNQUOTED); instead it reads the token's text as an unquoted value and attempts Long.parseLong on it, returning the parsed long when the parse succeeds.

A JSON generator's runtime toggling of the QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES feature is fully symmetric through the JsonGenerator enable()/disable() pair, so that after enable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES) and then disable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES), the quoting state of subsequently written field names returns to unquoted; disable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES) restores the unquoted behavior that a generator constructed with QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES disabled, and then enabled at runtime, would lose.

When DefaultPrettyPrinter.createInstance() is invoked on an instance whose runtime class is a proper subclass of DefaultPrettyPrinter (i.e. a subclass that has not overridden createInstance), it throws an IllegalStateException whose message includes the text "Failed `createInstance()`:", the subclass's class name, and a phrase stating that createInstance must be overridden.

When parsing an unquoted field name (Feature.ALLOW_UNQUOTED_FIELD_NAMES enabled) in ReaderBasedJsonParser on the secondary/buffer-continuation path (_handleOddName2), a character whose code-unit value equals the size of the JS-name lookup table `codes` (`codes.length`, 256) is no longer used to index that table; instead it is accepted into the field name if Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(char) is true for it, so that parsing such a name completes normally (no ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) and yields a FIELD_NAME token containing that character.

When writeValue() is invoked on an object-type context at a point where no field name is pending (a field name has not just been written that expects a value, e.g., right after the object started), writeValue() returns STATUS_EXPECT_NAME and does not advance the object's field state, instead of returning STATUS_OK_AFTER_COLON as before.

During AnyGetterWriter.resolve, if the installed any-getter serializer implements ContextualSerializer it is subjected to primary property contextualization (SerializersProvider.handlePrimaryContextualization) bound to the any-getter's bean property, and the output of that contextualization becomes the effective serializer used for the any-getter.

In deserializeUsingPropertyBasedWithUnwrapped, once all remaining trailing fields after the last creator property have been copied into the unwrapped buffer, if the parser's current token is not END_OBJECT, deserialization fails by reporting a wrong-token mismatch against expected token END_OBJECT with a message of the form "Attempted to unwrap '<handled type name>' value" rather than proceeding to write the end-object token and process unwrapped content.

When a TreeTraversingParser is positioned on a numeric value that cannot be converted to an int (node.canConvertToInt() is false), calling getLongValue() does not silently return node.longValue() but reports a long overflow: it throws a JsonParseException (InputCoercionException subtype) naming the value and 'out of range of long'. Consequence of the guard used: numeric long/BigInteger values that fit in a long but exceed int range also trigger this long-overflow report, because the double/long range check used is canConvertToInt() rather than canConvertToLong(). For a value that can convert to int, getLongValue() returns the value unchanged.

DefaultDeserializationContext.findObjectId(id, gen, resolver) returns null instead of proceeding to build an IdKey / look up / create and return a ReadableObjectId when the supplied id argument is null — a null object id is never wrapped in an IdKey, looked up in _objectIds, or used to create/register a ReadableObjectId.

When an ObjectReader binds JSON content as a JSON tree (the _bindAsTree path, used by ObjectReader.readTree(...) and by tree reads issued through the reader acting as a parser codec, e.g. JsonParser.readValueAsTree()), the root deserializer it uses is one for the JsonNode type resolved from the deserialization context and cached keyed by that JsonNode type; it must NOT be the reader's prefetched _rootDeserializer whenever that prefetched deserializer corresponds to some other (non-JsonNode) value type configured on the reader. Consequently, even a reader configured for a concrete value type (e.g. via readerForUpdating(bean) or forType(beanCls), where EAGER_DESERIALIZER_FETCH prefetches the bean deserializer) still performs correct tree deserialization — producing a faithful JsonNode rather than driving that bean deserializer over the JSON, which for a bean with a nested custom subtree-consuming deserializer previously caused the child subtree to be mis-consumed/mis-attributed.

ShortSerializer.isEmpty(prov, value) returns true if and only if value is a Short whose numeric value is its zero ((short) 0); it returns false for any non-zero Short and for null (since the constant 0 Short is compared with .equals).

For a non-null argument, TokenBuffer.writeString(String) and writeString(SerializableString) record the appended VALUE_STRING into the buffer's output write-context (a scalar value is committed / writeValue() is applied), so that getOutputContext() afterwards reflects that a value has been written in the same way the output context of a regular JsonGenerator does after the equivalent write (e.g. an enclosing array context has its written-value index advanced); writing a null String instead delegates to writeNull and is handled through that path. The tokens/length stored are otherwise unchanged.

When deserialize is invoked while the parser's current token is JsonToken.FIELD_NAME, the method consumes the entire enclosing object: it advances past the FIELD_NAME and repeatedly skips (discards) each value token it next encounters — the value bound to that field and the values of all following sibling fields of the same object — stopping only when nextToken returns null (end of input) or JsonToken.END_OBJECT, and then returns null without throwing. Observable consequence: parsing content after that enclosing object proceeds correctly because all of the object's content has been fully read/skipped.

When MapperFeature.AUTO_DETECT_GETTERS is disabled, DeserializationConfig.getDefaultVisibilityChecker() returns a VisibilityChecker whose getter visibility is set to Visibility.NONE (so getters are not auto-detected as properties during deserialization introspection).

When StdKeySerializers.EnumKeySerializer serializes an enum key and SerializationFeature.WRITE_ENUMS_USING_TO_STRING is enabled at serialization time, the field name is written as value.toString(), overriding any annotation-derived name; only when that feature is disabled is the introspector-derived/name() value written.

JavaType.withHandlersFrom(JavaType src) returns a JavaType that carries the same own-level type handler and value handler as `src` when those differ from this type's own handlers: the returned type's getTypeHandler() equals src.getTypeHandler() and getValueHandler() equals src.getValueHandler().

When a ValueInstantiator for a Collection returns true for canCreateUsingArrayDelegate() but getArrayDelegateType(config) returns null, collection deserialization setup aborts by throwing an IllegalArgumentException whose message starts with 'Invalid array-delegate-creator definition for ' and mentions both 'canCreateUsingArrayDelegate()' and 'null for 'getArrayDelegateType()''.

When a Reference's effective class (from _from, whether a Class value or an instance's runtime class) is an array type, the class-name segment rendered by getDescription() (and hence toString()) is the fully-qualified name of the array's innermost element/component class followed by one empty "[]" suffix per array dimension (e.g. an int[][].class reference yields "int[][]"; a String[].class reference yields "java.lang.String[]").

StdKeyDeserializer.forType recognizes CharSequence.class as a string-like key type (alongside String.class and Object.class) and returns a non-null StringKD key deserializer for it, instead of falling through to return null.

The set of types that Jackson refuses to deserialize by default contains each of the following class names: com.sun.org.apache.xalan.internal.xsltc.trax.TemplatesImpl, org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InstantiateTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections4.functors.InvokerTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections4.functors.InstantiateTransformer, org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.ConvertedClosure, org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.MethodClosure, and org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectFactory.

Calling getSuperClass() on a ResolvedRecursiveType whose referenced type has been resolved (via setReference) returns the result of _referencedType.getSuperClass() (i.e. the super class as seen through the resolved self-referential type's hierarchy), rather than the null/superClass field the placeholder itself carries.

When _typeFromId is resolving a type id that contains '<' (a generic/canonical type id), if the JavaType produced by constructFromCanonical(id) is not a type-or-subtype of the raw class of _baseType, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown rather than that non-subtype type being returned.

When a class supplied in the parameterClasses varargs of constructParametricType is itself a generic type whose hierarchy resolution needs to walk its type variables, that parameter class is now resolved with empty (non-null) type bindings and must not throw a NullPointerException from unbound type-variable resolution (previously it was resolved with null bindings).
When the InputStream argument is null, writeBinary writes a null value (the empty/self-closing element appropriate to the current context) and returns 0.

When parsing the portion following any combinator (`>`, ` `, `+`, `~`, `,`), an attribute-selector group written in balanced brackets [...] is consumed as a single atomic unit, so separator characters that are themselves combinator tokens (spaces, `>`, `~`, `+`, `,`) occurring inside the brackets (e.g. in the attribute value) do not terminate/split that sub-query; the whole bracketed expression remains part of the sub-query.

In parseByteData charset auto-detection (charsetName argument null), when the selected first meta carries an http-equiv attribute whose content does not resolve to a charset via getCharsetFromContentType, and the same meta also has a charset attribute naming a supported charset (that does not throw IllegalCharsetNameException on the support check), that charset-attribute value is used to re-decode the document instead of keeping the initial default-UTF-8 decoding; an unsupported or illegal-name charset attribute is ignored and the default decoding is retained.

When escaping with OutputSettings escape mode set to xhtml, a non-breaking space character (U+00A0) is emitted as the literal text ' ' (hex numeric character reference), rather than being appended as the raw U+00A0 character. This applies both in text-node and in-attribute escaping (the U+00A0 case is not guarded by the inAttribute flag).

When processing a non-Set-Cookie response header that occurs exactly once (values.size() == 1), the header is stored with that single value; the separately-added cases of zero or one value no longer lump multiple occurrences together as one.

XmlDeclaration.outerHtml()/toString() serializes the node as a complete, well-formed declaration: the opening prefix ('?' for an XML declaration where isProcessingInstruction is false, '!' where true), the declaration name, every attribute currently stored on the node (each emitted in insertion order by the standard attribute HTML serializer), then the matching closing prefix followed by '>'. Thus an xml declaration with attributes version, encoding and an extra custom attribute round-trips as e.g. '<?xml version="1" encoding="UTF-8" something="else"?>' (all attributes preserved, trailing '?' emitted); a node with no attributes renders as '<?xml?>' and not as the pre-fix malformed '<?xml>' that omitted the trailing marker.

TokenQueue.chompBalanced opens/closes its quote-tracking region only on un-escaped quote characters: a single- or double-quote character immediately preceded by a backslash (the escape char) does not toggle into or out of the quoted region, consistent with the existing backslash-escape handling for the balanced opener/closer characters.

In the InBody insertion mode's fall-through 'any other end tag' handling (used for end tags InBody doesn't treat specially), the end tag being closed is matched/used against open elements by the tag name exactly as written in the source (the case-preserved token name), so that when parsing with tag-name case preservation enabled (ParseSettings with preserveTagCase=true, e.g. ParseSettings.preserveCase) an open element whose stored tag case differs from lowercase (e.g. an uppercase custom element such as <X>...</X>) is correctly recognized and closed by its own matching-case close tag, rather than only ever being compared in always-lowercased form (as the pre-fix code did, which could not close such an element through this path).

For self-closing start tags of the InBody rawtext elements (<noembed />, <iframe />, <xmp />) that reach handleRawtext, the tokenising mode used for the remainder of the document is the normal Data mode (not Rawtext), i.e. content and tags following such an element are not absorbed as raw element data by the closed element.

When the parser is building a table section element (tbody, thead, or tfoot) - i.e. active/open-element context is within that table body, and a '<template>' start tag is parsed - the template element is inserted at the current position as a child of the section element that is currently open (and pushed onto the open-element stack without transitioning out), rather than being treated as non-table content and fostered out ahead of the table.

After an Element is cloned via clone(), a subsequent structural mutation of the clone's child-node list (for example appending a new descendant/sibling element) must invalidate and refresh the clone's own cached shadow child-elements list, so that element-tree queries that depend on that cache (e.g. nextElementSibling, previousElementSibling, children of the affected element) on the clone reflect the new child — behaving for later mutation queries the same as an equivalent independently-built element would.

After Document.normalise() runs on a document that contains more than one head element, all head elements except the first one in document order are removed and their child nodes are moved into that first, surviving head element, leaving exactly one head.

Evaluator.MatchText.matches returns true if and only if the candidate element is a PseudoTextElement; for any ordinary element it returns false (and, as described separately, performs a DOM restructuring).

StringUtil.isInvisibleChar(int c) returns true if and only if the codepoint c is one of 8203 (U+200B zero-width space), 8204 (U+200C zero-width non-joiner), 8205 (U+200D zero-width joiner), or 173 (U+00AD soft hyphen); it returns false for every other codepoint (including ordinary characters and whitespace).

When the XML parser processes a bogus comment whose data is longer than one character and begins with '!' or '?', and re-parsing the wrapped inner content ("<"+data.substring(1,len-1)+">") as an XML fragment yields a document with zero child nodes (i.e. the content cannot be parsed into an element), XmlTreeBuilder does not attempt to build an XmlDeclaration and does not raise an exception; the node inserted into the tree remains an ordinary Comment carrying the original comment text.

When parseInputStream parses a document using a charset whose canEncode() is false, the document's charset/encoding metadata element (HTML <meta charset> or XML encoding declaration) is updated/inserted to declare the default charset (UTF-8), making the serialized declaration consistent with the document's output charset.

Constructing a CharacterReader (via any of its constructors, since all delegate to CharacterReader(Reader, int) after the initial buffer-up) over input whose initially-buffered content contains 10 or more NUL ('\0') characters throws an UncheckedIOException with message "Input is binary and unsupported".

A node-type test with Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE (an XPath node() test) is satisfied by an org.jdom Document as well as an Element (i.e., this test returns true when evaluated against a JDOM document root).

When a comparison operand is a Pointer, the comparison always proceeds on that pointer's dereferenced value (getValue()); the prior fast path that treated two Pointers as equal (returning true) before inspecting their values is removed, so a two-pointer comparison is decided by comparing their dereferenced values via the standard type-based equality/inequality rules.

FastDateFormat.format(Date date) builds its calendar with the formatter's configured locale (mLocale), so that for patterns containing locale-sensitive numeric calendar fields whose computation depends on the calendar's first-day-of-week / minimal-days-in-first-week conventions (e.g. week-of-year from the 'w' rule and week-of-month from the 'W' rule), the output for a given Date reflects the formatter's locale's conventions rather than those of the JVM default locale.
ToStringStyle.isRegistered(value) returns false instead of throwing NullPointerException when the current thread's object registry is not set (i.e. when getRegistry() returns null).

NumberUtils.isNumber returns true for a string whose final character is a '.' that is the only decimal point (no earlier '.' and no exponent) and is preceded by at least one digit, e.g. isNumber("2.") == true.

When the IllegalArgumentException is thrown for an incompatible-array-type addAll call, its message is the exact string "Cannot store <array2 component type name> in an array of <array1 component type name>" (the names being the simple class names from getName(), e.g. "Cannot store java.lang.Long in an array of java.lang.Integer").

After being serialized and deserialized, a FastDateFormat instance remains fully functional: formatting a Date/Calendar/Long produces the same output as it did before serialization, and getMaxLengthEstimate() returns the same value as before serialization.

StrBuilder.indexOf(char ch, int startIndex) considers only indices from startIndex through the logical content boundary size-1 when searching, so it returns -1 (rather than a stale or beyond-content index) when ch does not occur within the logical content; it never reports a hit at an index >= size.

When the argument to compareTo is of a different runtime class whose binary name differs from the receiver's runtime class name (a genuinely different enum type), ValuedEnum.compareTo throws a ClassCastException whose message is "Different enum class '<short class name of other's class>'" rather than returning a value.

When the pattern of a newly built FastDateParser cannot be fully consumed by the format-field grammar (i.e. trailing pattern text — such as an unterminated single-quoted literal — remains unconsumed after tokenization), constructing the parser throws IllegalArgumentException (reporting that parsing 'Failed to parse' the pattern and the index where it gave up) rather than silently building a parser for the partially-consumed pattern.

For BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator): when the continued-fraction iteration produces a convergent whose numerator or denominator exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (overflow), if this occurs in max-denominator mode (epsilon == 0) and the previous convergent's denominator magnitude is strictly less than maxDenominator, construction no longer throws FractionConversionException; instead the constructor succeeds and returns the previous valid convergent (p1/q1).

After DSCompiler.atan2(y, yOffset, x, xOffset, result, resultOffset) returns, the 0th-order (value) element result[resultOffset] is set to FastMath.atan2(y[yOffset], x[xOffset]) for every input, thereby yielding the IEEE atan2 value in the special cases (+0/+0, +0/-0, -0/+0, -0/-0, and ±infinity combinations) where the branch-based derivative value computation produces an incorrect or NaN result.

When the least-squares problem's weight matrix is a DiagonalMatrix (the standard Weight-from-array case), the square-root-of-weight computation takes a diagonal path: the weight-matrix square root held by the optimizer is itself a DiagonalMatrix whose diagonal entries are FastMath.sqrt of the corresponding shared weight diagonal — so getWeightSquareRoot() returns a diagonal matrix of element-wise square roots, and the computation/storage stays linear in the number of targets instead of expanding into a dense matrix via a full eigendecomposition (so fitting a very large number of diagonal-weighted observations no longer exhausts memory/time).

In each reduction step of the pivoted rectangular Cholesky construction, the column selected for the next elimination is the remaining column with the largest current working-matrix diagonal element (correct maximal-element column pivoting). Concretely, the decomposition of the full-rank order-4 symmetric positive semidefinite covariance matrix reported in the issue (MATH-789 m1, threshold 1.0e-10) yields a root B with ||B·B^T − M|| at/near machine precision (~1e-16), instead of one corrupted by pivoting on a stale, out-of-date diagonal entry.

When the computed least-squares quantities take the direct, otherwise well-conditioned solution branch (both amplitude/omega ratios non-negative) yet the denominator coefficient c2 is exactly zero, the automatic parameter-guess procedure now aborts by throwing MathIllegalStateException (ZERO_DENOMINATOR) instead of silently continuing to evaluate a = sqrt(c1/c2) and omega = sqrt(c2/c3), which would divide by zero and yield NaN/Infinity parameter values.

During backward integration (target t before the current step start), in every trial-step attempt inside the local-error control loop, the step size is clamped so that the step never extends below the integration target: if stepStart + stepSize <= t, the step size is reduced to t - stepStart. As a consequence, no intermediate derivative evaluation for that trial step occurs at a time before t.

When, during acceptance of one integrator step that had multiple event handlers scheduled to occur (pending) inside it, the chronologically-first event's handler requests STOP so that acceptStep copies its interpolated state into y and returns that event's time early having marked the step as last, every other event handler that was also scheduled to occur later within the same candidate step is notified via stepAccepted at that same event time (with the copied state) before acceptStep returns, so none of the remaining handlers is left stepping from stale (pre-event) bracketing state.

The no-arg GaussianFitter.fit() computes its starting guess via GaussianFitter.ParameterGuesser.guess() on the current observations and uses exactly that guess as the initial parameter vector passed to the underlying curve fit; the resulting fitted parameter array (norm, mean, sigma — norm first, from the fitted optimum, not merely the guessed norm) is returned.

When a non-null VectorialConvergenceChecker is configured, doOptimize evaluates checker.converged against the last accepted trial's pair only (inside the successful-iteration branch), and applies no convergence-checker return on rejected probes; the checker is therefore never consulted about a rejected candidate.

A freshly constructed LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer has its vectorial convergence checker set to null (overriding the non-null SimpleVectorialValueChecker that the AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer superclass installs by default), so getConvergenceChecker() returns null after construction unless a checker is explicitly installed afterwards.

For an m×n input matrix with m<n whose compact/truncated SVD retains a positive-singular-value count p strictly less than m (rank deficiency or explicit truncation via constructor max), getV() returns an n×p right-singular factor computed from the full m-row eigenvector submatrix, so that when no truncation was applied the product getU()*getS()*getVT() recomposes the original matrix to within floating-point tolerance (instead of the last retained V column being computed without its secondary-bidiagonal coupling term and thereby causing the recomposition to diverge from the input).

Constructing a CholeskyDecompositionImpl on a symmetric matrix now throws NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException whenever the matrix is not positive definite as judged by the positivity threshold evaluated on the diagonal pivots during the Cholesky elimination — in particular, symmetric matrices whose original diagonal entries are all above the threshold but whose an updated elimination pivot (at any step) drops below the threshold (e.g. a non-SPD/non-semi-definite matrix for which a pivot becomes negative) are rejected instead of being silently decomposed into matrices containing NaN pivots.

getBasicRow still returns null when the column (below the objective rows) contains more than one non-zero non-epsilon entry (i.e. the degenerate / non-basic column detection over the scanned range is retained alongside the new unit-entry requirement).
DelegatingMethod.hashCode() returns the hash code of the wrapped java.lang.reflect.Method (rather than a constant), keeping it consistent with equals between equal DelegatingMethods.

ReturnsEmptyValues.returnValueFor(Iterable.class) (and therefore the default Answer for a mocked method whose declared return type is exactly Iterable) returns a newly created empty ArrayList rather than null, so the returned value is non-null, empty, and modifiable (no UnsupportedOperationException when code under test mutates it).

A deep-stub mock newly created as a method-call return value through ReturnsDeepStubs is Serializable (its creation settings include serializable()), so that mock object alone can be serialized and deserialized.

Reporter exposes two-argument smartNullPointerException(Object obj, Location location) (replacing the former single-Location overload) which throws a SmartNullPointerException whose message contains, in sequence among its joined lines: "You have a NullPointerException here:", a rendering of a freshly-created Location, the string representation of the passed obj argument, "Because this method was *not* stubbed correctly:", a rendering of the passed location, and a final empty line.

When SpyAnnotationEngine.process encounters a @Spy-annotated field whose value is a non-null instance that is not already a mock, it replaces the field value with a Mockito mock whose configured mock name is the field's own name, so that the created spy is referred to by that field name (e.g. in Mockito error/verification messages that print the mock's name) rather than by a generated default mock name.

When building the cannotInjectDependency failure message for a passed detail exception that has no cause, Reporter.exceptionCauseMessageIfAvailable returns that exception's own getMessage() (so cannotInjectDependency reports "Also I failed because: " + that message) instead of dereferencing a null cause and throwing a NullPointerException/similar.

During VerificationOverTimeImpl.verify's polling loop, an AssertionError thrown by delegate.verify(data) that is NOT a MockitoAssertionError (e.g. a plain java.lang.AssertionError or any AssertionError subtype other than MockitoAssertionError and the JUnit-flavoured ArgumentsAreDifferent) is no longer allowed to propagate immediately out of verify; it is now passed to handleVerifyException and thereby subjected to the recoverability/retry logic — i.e. stored as the accumulated error and, if the delegate can recover, slept/retried until the timer elapses (only then rethrown), rather than escaping from the very first polling iteration it occurs in.

calculatePrintedLength for a SECONDS_MILLIS or SECONDS_OPTIONAL_MILLIS field returns a length that reflects the extra minus sign that printTo(StringBuffer,...) emits for a negative combined value (i.e. it uses a one-larger baseline for negative combined values than for non-negative ones), so the computed printed length matches the actual emitted string length, including for the negative-sub-second case.

DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, String, int) uses the year of the supplied instant as the default year when parsing text that supplies day-scale fields (e.g. month and day) without a year, so the resulting instant's year is taken from the instant being populated rather than from the formatter's configured default year.

When parseInto parses text that specifies some fields but omits the year (fields whose duration is between a month and a day, e.g. month-only or month/day), the default year given to the parse bucket — the year into whose context the parsed non-year fields resolve — is derived from the input instant's epoch millis getMillis() read via that instant's own chronology, NOT from its zone-offset-shifted local millis (instant.getMillis() + zone offset) and NOT in an override chronology/zone-selected context; consequently an input instant whose offset/local calendar year would fall one year away from its epoch-millis year (e.g. late-December UTC instants in a large positive-offset zone whose local time has already rolled into January of the next year) has its parsed year-defaulted fields resolved against the epoch year rather than the adjacent shifted year.

DateTimeZone.forOffsetMillis(int millisOffset) throws IllegalArgumentException (whose message includes the offending value) when millisOffset is outside the closed interval from -86,399,999 ms (-23:59:59.999) to +86,399,999 ms (+23:59:59.999), i.e. whenever its magnitude is at least a full day (86,400,000 ms); in-range millis offsets still resolve to the corresponding fixed-offset zone.
`pysnooper.pycompat` exposes a module-level boolean attribute `PY2` whose value is the logical negation of the existing `PY3` attribute (True on Python 2, False on Python 3).

get_write_function(output), when output is a str or a pycompat.PathLike, returns a callable that appends each string it is called with to a file opened at the path given by the output argument itself (rather than at the undefined name output_path, which raised NameError before the fix).
The `collections` FieldAttribute of CollectionSearch is marked as a static attribute, so it is never templated during post-validation; the value is used as-is.

When check_required_arguments finds one or more required parameters missing, the raised TypeError's message lists the missing parameter names in sorted (lexicographic) order (e.g. 'missing required arguments: a, b, c').

ShellModule.join_path collapses repeated/duplicate directory separators inside an argument, so a path fragment containing doubled slashes is emitted with a single separator (leading UNC double-backslash excepted).

Rhsm.subscribe_by_pool_ids passes the pool quantity to subscription-manager as a native string (converted with to_native), so a non-string quantity value (e.g. an int) appears in the command argv as its string form.
The cleanup path of `black.reformat_many` calls `executor.shutdown()` only when `executor is not None`, so a run that fell back to a `None` executor does not raise `AttributeError` during cleanup.
In Driver._partially_consume_prefix, a tab character in the prefix advances the tracked indentation column by exactly 1, i.e. a tab is counted the same as a space rather than as 4 columns.

When BracketTracker.mark processes a leaf that is the NAME token 'for', it increases the tracker's depth by one for the tokens that follow, so that leaves between 'for' and its matching 'in' on a line are treated as being one level deeper (and thus their comma delimiters are not split on).

The async-def state used for async/await tokenization is only entered when the stashed `async` is immediately followed by `def`; an `async for` does not enable that state (so subsequent `async`/`await` occurrences outside an `async def` are not tokenized as ASYNC/AWAIT).

When the platform default encoding differs from UTF-8, the temporary log file produced by black.dump_to_file contains the dumped text encoded as UTF-8 bytes rather than in the platform default encoding.

Line.append_comment returns False without recording the comment when the line has no leaves (the comment would be first); in that case the comment's type is set to STANDALONE_COMMENT and its prefix is set to the empty string.

When Black splits a line, the body lines produced for imports and for function definitions whose bracketed body contains no comma token are ensured to end with a trailing comma: `bracket_split_build_line` inserts a `,` immediately after the last non-comment leaf of such a body (skipping any trailing standalone comments), so a split single-argument function definition renders its argument followed by a comma before the closing bracket.
black.Feature exposes two new mutually-exclusive members, ASYNC_IS_VALID_IDENTIFIER and ASYNC_IS_RESERVED_KEYWORD.

The decision to wrap the first testlist_star_expr child in invisible parentheses is triggered by the child's position (index 0) and node type, independent of whether the previous leaf's value was in parens_after, so a statement like `a, b = ...` (with no preceding assignment leaf marker) still gets its tuple target wrapped.

When bracket_split_build_line builds the body of a split import line (is_body=True and original.is_import) and none of the leaves is a COMMA, a comma leaf is inserted immediately after the last leaf that is not a STANDALONE_COMMENT, so the comma always precedes any trailing standalone-comment leaves (a comma is never placed after a standalone comment / at the very end of the list when a trailing standalone comment exists).

get_grammars(target_versions) with a non-empty target_versions set that contains at least one Python 2 version (e.g. {TargetVersion.PY27}) returns a list of exactly two grammars, in the order (python_grammar_no_print_statement, python_grammar) — i.e. the Python 3-style no-print-statement grammar is attempted first and the full Python 2 grammar second.
APIRouter.include_router propagates each included APIRoute's response_model_exclude_defaults and response_model_exclude_none values to the newly created route.

When HTTPBearer is constructed with auto_error=False and the request lacks an Authorization header or lacks a scheme/credentials, HTTPBearer.__call__ returns None (this behavior is unchanged by the patch and is preserved for the auto_error=False configuration).

SchemaBase.additionalProperties no longer accepts values that are neither a boolean nor a mapping (e.g. a bare string, number, or list); such values fail validation instead of being passed through unconstrained as before (the previous Union[bool, Any] allowed any value).
The path of a copied websocket route is the concatenation of the include_router prefix and the original route's path (prefix + route.path).

jsonable_encoder, when given a pydantic BaseModel whose Config does not define a `json_encoders` attribute, does not raise AttributeError but instead encodes the model by falling back to the caller-supplied `custom_encoder`.

_prepare_response_content recurses into list values, returning a new list in which each element has been prepared, so BaseModels nested inside a list response are also converted (with aliases / exclude_unset applied) rather than being passed through as model instances.

create_cloned_field, when cloning a ModelField whose type is a BaseModel subclass, produces a new model type whose __fields__ entries are themselves the result of create_cloned_field applied to each of the original model's fields (i.e. the cloned model's fields are recursively cloned rather than being the original model's field objects).

In Model.fit_generator, when validation_data is a keras.utils.Sequence and validation is run without worker processes (workers == 0), an explicitly supplied truthy validation_steps value is preserved unchanged and is not overridden by len(validation_data).

CSVLogger opens its output file through io.open(filename, mode + self.file_flags, **self._open_args), i.e. with the file object's newline translation parameter supplied by the callback rather than by the platform default.

When a Function is constructed with run_metadata=... on a TensorFlow version older than 1.10 (and inputs are not symbolic tensors, and inputs are not sparse), calling the Function executes via the legacy session.run path rather than the callable path, and returns the same output values as the callable path.

Conv2DTranspose.__init__ accepts a dilation_rate argument (default (1, 1)) and forwards it to the parent Conv2D/_Conv constructor so that the constructed layer's self.dilation_rate reflects the supplied value (normalized to a 2-tuple), instead of always being (1, 1).

Bidirectional.get_updates_for(inputs) returns the concatenation of the Bidirectional layer's own updates (registered on itself for the given inputs, via Layer.get_updates_for), the forward_layer's updates for those inputs, and the backward_layer's updates for those inputs; previously the wrapper's inherited implementation consulted only the originally passed layer, so the forward/backward sublayers' updates never appeared.
Model.compile creates and initializes the attribute self.stateful_metric_functions to an empty list during compilation.

On Python 3, text_to_word_sequence replaces every character in `filters` with the full `split` string before splitting, so that when `split` is multi-character the filtered characters are substituted by the whole split string, not by individual characters.

process_list_block, when the docstring contains no blank line ('\n\n') at or after starting_point, limits the extracted block to docstring[starting_point:section_end] (end of the section / next section heading) instead of extending the block to the end of the docstring, so text belonging to later parts of the docstring is not included in the returned block.
The scheduler config parameter `disable_hard_timeout` defaults to 999999999 (rather than None) when not supplied via kwargs or config.

Instantiating a concrete BeamDataflowJobTask subclass whose dataflow_params is a DataflowParamKeys instance also runs the luigi.Task constructor (super().__init__()), so the constructed task is a fully initialized luigi.Task (e.g. task_id/task_family are populated) rather than a task on which luigi.Task.__init__ was never called.

Task.to_str_params() returns a dict containing an entry for every parameter the task was constructed with, including parameters declared with significant=False; no parameter is omitted on the basis of its significance.
Constructing Worker(worker_id) without passing last_active results in worker.last_active being a numeric (float) epoch timestamp rather than None.
The scheduler config exposes a boolean parameter `prune_on_get_work` (accessibly as an attribute of the scheduler Config object) that defaults to False.

SparkSubmitTask._dict_arg, when given a name and a non-empty dict, emits for each key/value entry the pair [name, 'prop=value'] with the formatted 'prop=value' text carrying no surrounding double quotes (previously the value was wrapped as '"prop=value"').

When run_job is invoked without SSH configuration and the job's jar() returns a falsy value (e.g. None or ''), it raises HadoopJarJobError with the message "Jar not defined" instead of attempting to check the path, and never calls os.path.exists on the jar value.

Parameter.parse_from_input accepts an optional third argument task_name (keyword-or-positional, defaulting to None) in addition to param_name and x, so callers may request a task-name-aware default resolution; calling it with only (param_name, x) remains valid.

Register.__get_reg()/Register.task_names() include every registered Task subclass regardless of whether it overrides run: a class whose run attribute is the inherited, non-overridden value is no longer omitted from the registry listing. Observable via task_names() listing such a class and get_task_cls(name) resolving it.
The luigi.task_register module exposes a module-level logger object bound to a logging.Logger named 'luigi-interface' (created via logging.getLogger('luigi-interface')).

_recursively_freeze converts a tuple value (and any tuple nested inside a Mapping or sequence) into a tuple of recursively-frozen elements, in the same way it already does for lists, rather than returning the tuple unchanged.

matplotlib.transforms.nonsingular handles integer-typed (e.g. numpy integer) vmin/vmax endpoints correctly: it does not produce an incorrect result due to integer overflow or wraparound (such as `abs(np.int8(-128))` evaluating to -128, or `vmax - vmin` overflowing), and instead applies the normal singularity-expansion logic as if the endpoints were floats.
In Axes.scatter, an unfilled marker continues to force edgecolors to 'face' regardless of the linewidths supplied.

Index.get_indexer_non_unique, when both the calling index and the target are all-dates (self.is_all_dates is True and target.is_all_dates is True), continues to derive the target values from target.asi8, so datetime-index-to-datetime-index lookups are unchanged.
Categorical.min on an empty (zero-length) ordered Categorical returns the dtype's NA value (NaN) instead of raising an error or returning a category.

Index.get_value raises InvalidIndexError(key) when the values of `series` are an ExtensionArray and `key` is not a scalar (e.g. an ndarray/list of labels), rather than falling through to a numpy-based lookup of the values.

The margins adjustment does not raise for the previously handled non-reshapable index case: when the append of the margin row fails, the result index is coerced with _to_safe_for_reshape and the margin row is then appended, and the original index names are restored on the returned result.

DataFrame.corr (all methods) operates on a float64 NumPy representation of the numeric-only columns obtained via DataFrame.astype(float, copy=False) followed by to_numpy(), so nullable/extension-array numeric columns (e.g. Int64Dtype with pd.NA) are accepted without raising a conversion error.

GroupBy._reindex_output accepts an optional `fill_value` argument (default np.NaN) and uses that scalar as the fill value for entries created by the categorical-group-expansion reindex: in the as_index=True branch it is forwarded to `output.reindex`, and in the as_index=False branch it is forwarded to the `output.set_index(...).reindex(index, ...)` call.

ObjectBlock._replace_coerce, when the given boolean mask contains no True entries but convert is truthy, returns a single-element list containing the block converted via convert(numeric=False, copy=True) (rather than returning the unchanged block itself).

When several rows of the intermediate percentage-change result share the same index label, NDFrame.pct_change keeps the first such row for that label and discards the later ones (rather than raising or keeping all of them).

When a scalar np.datetime64 operand is subtracted from a timedelta64-dtype DatetimeLikeArrayMixin (e.g. `np.datetime64(t) - TimedeltaArray`/`TimedeltaIndex`), __rsub__ returns the result of `Timestamp(other) - self` (a datetime64-dtype array of Timestamps) rather than attempting to wrap the scalar in DatetimeArray; this holds for the scalar np.datetime64('NaT') as well, yielding all-NaT entries.
pandas.core.dtypes.missing._isna_ndarraylike accepts a keyword argument `old` (bool) that defaults to False, so existing callers can invoke it without the argument and get the non-inf-as-NA behavior.
Series.var() on a timedelta64-dtype Series raises TypeError matching "operation 'var' not allowed" (for both empty and non-empty timedelta Series), instead of returning a Timedelta/NaT.
_coerce_to_type casts boolean-dtype input to int64, so that boolean data reaching cut/qcut is treated as numeric 0/1 data instead of a bool array.

_normalize raises ValueError with the message "<margins_name> not in pivoted DataFrame" when margins is True and the given margins label is neither a component of the last row's index name nor equal to the last column's label (i.e. the margins label is not positioned as the final row/column of the table).

For input containing no infinite values, `_Window._prep_values` may return the same array object it was given (no coercion/copy is forced just to handle infinities), so operations on the returned value preserve the original data and dtype.
Index instances expose a `_supports_partial_string_indexing` attribute that is False by default on the base Index class.

For the empty-column-collection early return of DataFrame.quantile, the empty Index used for the result's column axis (the Series' index, or the DataFrame's columns) carries the name of the calling frame's columns axis, i.e. self.columns.name, and the result's axis labels are otherwise empty.

Calling a rolling aggregation named 'skew' with a BaseIndexer subclass as the window (e.g. df.rolling(<BaseIndexer>).skew()) no longer raises NotImplementedError; 'skew' is treated as supported so the computation proceeds and returns a result.

Indexing with .loc using a 1-D list-like of scalar (non-tuple) labels against an axis whose labels are a MultiIndex resolves the labels against level 0 of that axis (a reindex-like multi-selection; for a Series/ndarray key it is the key's values, not its own index, that are used), and raises KeyError with a message containing 'not in index' when any requested label is not present, instead of silently ignoring the missing labels and returning only the rows/columns whose labels were found.

MonthOffset.apply_index returns a DatetimeIndex constructed from the shifted i8 values without passing the input index's freq (i.e. the input `i.freq` is not forwarded to `_simple_new`); only `dtype` is forwarded.
DatetimeArray.isocalendar continues to return a DataFrame with columns ['year', 'week', 'day'] and UInt32 dtype, with NaT positions set to None, unchanged in structure by the timezone handling.

_factorize_keys accepts a `how` keyword argument (default "inner"); when called with how="right" it returns the right key's labels first and the left key's labels second (i.e. (rlab, llab, count) instead of (llab, rlab, count)); for any other `how` value it returns (llab, rlab, count) as before.
DatetimeIndexOpsMixin defines a `_is_comparable_dtype(dtype)` predicate that raises AbstractMethodError when called (it is abstract, to be overridden by the concrete datetime-like index subclasses).

Assigning via .loc with a label indexer whose column part is a list-like containing labels not present in the columns, e.g. df.loc[:, ['a', 'newcol']] = values, no longer raises for the missing labels: the missing labels are first created as NaN-filled columns, and the assignment then proceeds normally.

In DataFrameGroupBy._cython_agg_blocks, when a block is an extension-dtype block and the aggregated result is an ndarray, if re-casting the result via type(block.values)._from_sequence(result.ravel(), dtype=block.values.dtype) raises a ValueError, the exception is swallowed and the result is instead reshaped to (1, -1) so it is a valid input for a non-Extension Block.

The ValueError message raised by CategoricalDtype._from_values_or_dtype for an unrecognized non-string, non-CategoricalDtype `dtype` is f"Cannot not construct CategoricalDtype from {dtype}" (the repr of the offending dtype object interpolated into the message).

DataFrame._get_value(..., takeable=True) obtains its column Series through DataFrame._ixs(col, axis=1), so the retrieved column Series is the frame's cached column Series for that positional column (it is marked as cached against `self`, and is named after the column label).

Series.__getitem__ with a non-scalar key that infers as integer-valued, when the Series index is not integer-, floating-, or IntervalIndex-typed, returns the same object as positional indexing with Series.iloc[key]: a Series whose values are taken by position and whose labels are the corresponding entries of self.index, rather than the result of the internal self._get_values(key) slice path (which could raise a slice-specific error or return a bare numpy array instead of a Series).

For scalar .at access, an integer key on an axis that is neither integer-holding nor floating (e.g. an object/string index) still raises ValueError with the message 'At based indexing on an non-integer index can only have non-integer indexers'.
The integer-extension-array handling in pandas.cut applies for all forms of bins: a scalar int, a sequence of bin edges, and an IntervalIndex all work with an integer-dtype extension array as x.

A replace call on a block whose match mask is empty does not take an early no-op shortcut: Block.replace still produces its result through the putmask-based replacement path (and, when convert=True, the post-replacement convert step) rather than returning the original block/its copy.

_Concatenator._get_comb_axis passes the concatenator's copy flag (self.copy, set from the concat(copy=...) argument) through to get_objs_combined_axis, so pd.concat(copy=True) results in a copied non-concatenation axis index while pd.concat(copy=False) does not.

Categorical.__contains__ returns self.isna().any() (i.e. True iff the Categorical contains at least one missing value) when key is a scalar NA value that is valid for the Categorical's categories dtype, as determined by is_valid_nat_for_dtype(key, self.categories.dtype); for example `np.nan in cat` is True exactly when the Categorical has any NaN value.

PeriodIndex.searchsorted raises TypeError with a message containing "requires either a Period or PeriodArray" for any argument that is not a Period, NaT, str, or PeriodArray (e.g. an int64 ndarray, a timedelta64 array, a timedelta64 scalar, a datetime64 scalar).

pandas.core.indexes.datetimelike exposes the names DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray, imported from pandas.core.arrays (so that DatetimeIndex/TimedeltaIndex underlying arrays can be tested with isinstance against those classes inside this module).

Comparing a Period-backed array (PeriodArray / PeriodIndex / period-dtype Series) with an integer scalar no longer performs an element-wise comparison against a Period constructed from that integer and the array's freq; instead the integer scalar falls through the non-list-like path and yields an invalid-comparison result.

For a Location header given as bytes that encode non-ASCII characters, the resulting redirected request URL percent-encodes those bytes using their raw byte values (so latin1-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%E7%E3o' and UTF-8-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%C3%A7%C3%A3o'), rather than percent-encoding UTF-8 of the latin1-decoded code points.
response_status_message(status) returns a string of the form '<status> Unknown Status' when the status code has no entry in the HTTP reason-phrase mapping, instead of raising an exception.

When FormRequest.from_response is called without an explicit url and the form has no 'action' attribute, the resulting request URL is the form's base URL resolved against the document base URL (i.e. the response URL, or the page's <base href> if present), rather than the raw action attribute.

When a `<name>_BASE` setting exists, `_getcomposite(name)` builds the composite from the `<name>_BASE` entries and from those entries of `self[name]` whose stored priority is strictly greater than the 'default' priority; entries of `self[name]` whose priority equals 'default' are NOT included in the returned composite even though they are present in `self[name]`.

WrappedRequest.get_header returns the header value converted to a native string using error replacement, so a header value whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 yields a string with the undecodable bytes replaced (U+FFFD) instead of raising a UnicodeDecodeError.

The deprecation warning emitted by Spider.start_requests is formatted to include, in '<module>.<classname>' form, the __module__ and __name__ of the concrete class of the spider instance on which start_requests() was called (i.e. the dynamic class, not always Spider).
_get_form_url(form, None), when the form element has no 'action' attribute, returns form.base_url unchanged (rather than attempting URL resolution on a missing action value).

When the split command parts contain the standalone token '--set-upstream', git_push.get_new_command builds the corrected command from the command script with that token and the single token immediately following it removed.

Fish._get_overridden_aliases() returns a set of alias names (a Python set, not a list), so its result compares equal to a set literal of the same names and supports set semantics (e.g. `isinstance`/`type` check reports set).
Bash.get_aliases() returns an empty dict (rather than raising KeyError) when TF_SHELL_ALIASES is not set in the environment.

dirty_unzip.get_new_command builds the corrected command as '<original script> -d <archive name without .zip>', shell-escaping that destination directory via shells.quote, so a directory name containing shell-special characters is emitted quoted and remains a single argument; for ordinary names the output is unchanged (e.g. 'unzip foo' -> 'unzip foo -d foo', 'unzip foo.zip' -> 'unzip foo.zip -d foo').

repr(CorrectedCommand(script, side_effect, priority)) produces the string 'CorrectedCommand(script={script}, side_effect={side_effect}, priority={priority})' with the three attribute values interpolated.

Settings.update(**kwargs) returns a new settings object in which, for any key present in both the receiver and kwargs, the receiver's existing value is retained and the kwargs value is ignored; calling Settings({'key': 'val'}).update(key='new-val') yields a result whose 'key' attribute equals 'val'.
ls_lah.match returns True when command.script is exactly 'ls' (no trailing space or arguments).
_get_aliases parses alias lines of the form `alias <name>=<value>` (separated by an equals sign, with no space available to split on) into a `name: value` entry.

match() returns True only when command.output contains both the substring "fatal: A branch named '" and the substring "' already exists." (i.e. the closing single quote before " already exists." is required); for an output like "fatal: A branch named 'foo already exists." (no closing quote) match() returns False.
_get_operations reads the dnf help output from the subprocess stdout and decodes it as UTF-8 before parsing, so the text passed to _parse_operations is a str (not bytes).

FacebookGraphMixin._on_access_token derives the session's access_token (and expires) entries from the access-token response body using the standard query-string parser (urlparse.parse_qs) rather than escape.parse_qs_bytes, so on Python 3 the resulting session values are native text strings rather than latin1-decoded byte strings.

WaitIterator.next() registers a done-callback on the Future it returns (the running future) that holds a strong reference to the WaitIterator, so that the WaitIterator is not garbage-collected while that returned future is still pending even when the caller retains no other reference to it.

AsyncHTTPClient.close() does not raise RuntimeError when the per-IOLoop instance-cache slot for self.io_loop holds the value None (e.g. when the entry was cleared by a weakref before a destructor-driven close runs); the call returns normally and leaves the client marked closed.

When a WebSocket client request is missing or has invalid required headers (Host, Sec-Websocket-Key, Sec-Websocket-Version), WebSocketProtocol13.accept_connection responds with HTTP status code 400 instead of aborting the connection.
When total is known and a progress bar is rendered but ncols is falsy (None or 0), format_meter returns the fully formatted meter string 'res' (untrimmed) instead of returning None.

tqdm.format_meter does not raise an exception when called with a falsy (None or 0) total together with a custom numeric unit_scale (unit_scale not in (True, 1)); it returns the stats-only formatted string instead.

The number of returned formats includes a distinct entry for every processed video/audio Representation, so duplicate representation ids produce duplicate (same format_id) entries rather than being collapsed into a single entry.
When path is a bytes object that fails to decode as UTF-8, urljoin propagates the decoding error instead of returning None.

js_to_json recognizes a hexadecimal (0x/0X...) or octal (0 followed by octal digits) numeric literal only when it starts at a word boundary; when the leading '0' is immediately preceded by a word character (letter, digit, or underscore) the sequence is not treated as a number literal and is left unconverted (e.g. js_to_json('10xff') leaves '10xff' rather than producing '1255'), while a literal that does start at a word boundary is still converted to its decimal form as before (e.g. '{0xff:0xff}' still maps to {'255': 255}, and '{077:077}' still maps to {'63': 63}).

parse_dfxp_time_expr accepts a clock-form timestamp whose seconds component uses a colon as the fractional separator (e.g. 'HH:MM:SS:sss'), returning the corresponding number of seconds as a float; previously such input produced None.

FacebookIE still matches all URLs that matched before the change, including (a) URLs with no '#!' fragment at all such as 'https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?v=120708114770723' and (b) URLs whose pre-fragment prefix contains no '?' such as 'https://www.facebook.com/foo#!/video/video.php?v=123'.

youtube_dl.utils exposes a function urlencode_postdata that URL-encodes its arguments (forwarding *args/**kargs to compat_urllib_parse.urlencode) and returns the result encoded as an ASCII bytes object rather than a str.

JSInterpreter.interpret_expression accepts a JS function-call expression with an empty argument list, e.g. 'x()', as a valid supported expression rather than falling through to 'Unsupported JS expression'.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a function named fix_xml_ampersands(xml_str) that takes an XML string and returns a string.

unified_timestamp, when the input date string fails every date_formats() strptime pattern and is instead parsed by email.utils.parsedate_tz, now includes a 12-hour (43200-second) positive offset in the returned UNIX timestamp whenever the original input contains 'PM' (case-insensitive), so e.g. unified_timestamp('May 16, 2016 11:15 PM') returns the PM-corrected timestamp rather than the AM one.
parse_dfxp_time_expr returns None (not 0.0) when time_expr is falsy (empty string, None, or 0).

YoutubeDL.build_format_selector accepts a format specification that combines a '/' choice with a top-level ',' list at the same nesting level (e.g. 'bestvideo/best,worst') and returns a usable format-selector function without raising an error.

In a format specification, the right-hand operand of the '+' (merge) operator terminates at an unparenthesized '/' or ',' instead of absorbing it, so '/' and ',' bind looser than '+': e.g. 'bestvideo+bestaudio/best' selects the pick-first between the merged 'bestvideo+bestaudio' pair and 'best', rather than merging bestvideo with the choice (bestaudio/best).

When reading a table from a filename or file-like input with memmap=True, invalid-value masking (NaNs in float/complex columns and empty strings in character columns) is unconditionally disabled: mask_invalid is set to False regardless of the caller-supplied value of the mask_invalid argument.

Constructing a Time with format='byear' from a value that is a genuine quantity (exposes a 'to' method and a non-None 'unit') still raises ValueError with the message 'Cannot use Quantities for \'byear\' format...', but a value that happens to expose 'to' and 'unit' attributes whose unit is None is no longer rejected and is instead handled as an ordinary numeric Besselian-year input.

When called with as_image_hdu=True, fits_ccddata_writer (reached via CCDData.write) writes the CCDData data into an ImageHDU extension while prepending an effectively data-free PrimaryHDU as element 0 of the written FITS file, so the file's first HDU is a PrimaryHDU and the data lives in the following ImageHDU; when as_image_hdu is False or omitted, the file is written as before with the data in the PrimaryHDU.

Cosmology read/write I/O offers 'ascii.html' as a registered format: once astropy.cosmology.io is imported (which now imports io.html), Cosmology.read and Cosmology.write accept format='ascii.html' and Cosmology.read with no format can auto-identify an ascii.html file by its '.html' filename suffix.

astropy.utils.metadata.common_dtype returns a dtype representation that preserves the named fields (the resulting ndarray dtype's .descr, a list of (name, dtype-spec, shape) tuples) instead of the lossy .str void-form whenever the common dtype computed across the input arrays has named fields (i.e. arr_common.dtype.names is not None).

An Angle whose unit is specified as hours (u.hour or an hour unit that compares equal to u.hour) is normalized to hourangle, so that to_string() of such an angle (or when u.hour is passed as the to_string unit) yields hourangle/hms sexagesimal rather than being treated as a non-degree, non-hour-angle angular unit.

Indexing a Quantity whose unit is a StructuredUnit with a string field key (returning the sub-quantity corresponding to that field) produces a result that does not inherit the source quantity's per-instance `info`; only the field's unit is assigned to the new view.

When a WCS is constructed from a header whose (default-key) CTYPE codes end in '-TAN' on exactly two axes and at least one of those '-TAN' axes carries a PV keyword with subscript j >= 5, those CTYPE codes are rewritten to end in '-TPV' in the resulting core WCS (so the WCS uses the TPV projection) and the SIP distortion is not loaded (the resulting WCS.sip is None), while a FITSFixedWarning with message 'Removed redundant SIP distortion parameters because SCAMP' PV distortions are also present' is emitted.

write_latex accepts a 'format' keyword argument of 'ascii.latex' in addition to 'latex' (previously any value other than exactly 'latex' was rejected), and for either accepted value it writes the LaTeX table output normally; a 'format' value other than 'latex' or 'ascii.latex' raises ValueError with the message "format must be 'latex' or 'ascii.latex', not {format}".
