An app-label argument that refers to an app which is installed in INSTALLED_APPS but has no migrations is no longer treated as an error: validation only rejects labels that fail apps.get_app_config (non-installed), so such an installed-but-unmigrated app no longer causes the process to raise an error or exit non-zero for that reason.

For a non-add object change with non-empty changed form data, the returned change_message's top-level {'changed': {'fields': [...]}} entry must list each changed form field by its verbose label rather than its raw attribute name — each label being the corresponding form field's .label, with the raw field name used when that field has no (empty) .label or is not present as a field on the form.

For a Media produced by summing other Media objects (m1 + m2 + ... + mn, in any nesting/grouping of the + operations), each CSS output medium's path list is built by merging that medium's paths across the css dictionaries of the base operands in their source addition order — a css medium appearing in any operand is present in the result, later-operand paths that duplicate earlier ones are not re-added, empty css members are inert, and parenthesization of the sum does not change any medium's resulting path list.

Running the system checks on a BinaryField that has an explicit default which is a str (e.g. BinaryField(default='') or any other str default) returns a checks.Error with id 'fields.E170' and obj set to that field.

AutoField.get_prep_value, when the value passed after super().get_prep_value is not None and not an OuterRef and cannot be converted by int(value), raises an exception of the same class as the one int(value) raised (TypeError or ValueError), whose message is "Field '%s' expected a number but got %r." % (self.name, value), with the original conversion error chained via 'from e'.

When django.utils.http.urlencode is called with queries whose direct mapping value for a key is None (the outer loop guard, regardless of doseq), the TypeError raised has message "Cannot encode None for key '<key>' in a query string. Did you mean to pass an empty string or omit the value?", where '<key>' is replaced with the offending key.
ManifestFilesMixin's constructor accepts a keyword argument manifest_storage and stores it on the instance as the manifest_storage attribute.

When resolving a 'pk' ordering lookup (the pk shortcut), if the model's pk is a relation field (e.g. the parent pointer under multi-table inheritance) pointing to a model that declares its own Meta.ordering, SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name treats the lookup as an order-by-the-pk-column clause rather than substituting the referenced model's Meta.ordering in its place.

CommandError instances expose a `returncode` attribute whose value is 1 by default and can be set through a `returncode=` keyword argument to the constructor; this applies to every CommandError (and, via inheritance, to subclasses such as SystemCheckError that do not override __init__).

MigrationLoader.__init__ accepts a replace_migrations keyword argument whose default value is True, so that MigrationLoader(connection) (and callers like MigrationExecutor) keeps the previous default collapsing behavior.

When make_password raises TypeError for a non-bytes/str, non-None password, the exception message uses the __qualname__ of the passed password's type in the text 'Password must be a string or bytes, got <qualname>.'

DatabaseOperations.sql_flush's signature is changed (in base and every backend) from (style, tables, sequences, allow_cascade) to (style, tables, *, reset_sequences=False, allow_cascade=False): the positional sequences argument is removed and sequence-reset behavior is instead requested via the keyword-only reset_sequences boolean (default False). Passing a sequences argument positionally now raises a TypeError.

When `loader.check_consistent_history(connection)` for a per-connection history check raises `django.db.OperationalError`, the `makemigrations` command no longer lets that exception abort execution; instead it catches it and continues to run to normal completion (conflict detection and onward), so the command does not exit with an error solely because a database connection could not be reached.

When the configured session engine's SESSION_ENGINE module exposes a SessionStore whose clear_expired() raises NotImplementedError, running/executing the clearsessions command raises django.core.management.base.CommandError whose message is exactly "Session engine '<SESSION_ENGINE>' doesn't support clearing expired sessions.", causing the command to fail (non-zero return code) rather than writing a message to stderr and completing normally.

When SessionMiddleware.process_response takes the session-deletion branch (SESSION_COOKIE_NAME present in request cookies and session empty), the deletion cookie is now written with samesite=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, so the emptied session cookie carries the SameSite attribute from the SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting.

In MigrationLoader.load_disk, once an app's migrations module is confirmed to be a regular (non-namespace) package (it has both a __file__ and a __path__), the app's label is added to migrated_apps unconditionally — the previously conditional logic that would instead add it to unmigrated_apps when the package contained no migration submodules and ignore_no_migrations was False is removed, so an app with a real but empty migrations package is now treated as migrated regardless of the number of migration submodules it contains and regardless of the ignore_no_migrations value.

When autodetection changes an already-existing (kept) model whose `order_with_respect_to` option changes and which simultaneously has index/unique/index_together/constraint/db-table changes to emit, the `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` operation for that model is generated (and therefore ordered) before the added-index, altered-unique-together, altered-index-together, added-constraint, and altered-db-table operations belonging to the same autodetection run, so schema referencing the ordering's `_order` column is not added ahead of the ordering operation.

TemplateView.get passes the keyword arguments it receives from dispatch (URLconf-captured URL kwargs) directly into the template context, so each URL keyword argument name maps in the rendered context to its ordinary raw value, no longer wrapped in a lazy/deferred object.

A combined arithmetic expression (CombinedExpression using ADD, SUB, MUL or DIV) whose two source sub-expressions have output fields that are integer-kind fields — i.e. any pair that are each IntegerField or an IntegerField subclass such as AutoField, SmallAutoField or BigAutoField (distinct classes, e.g. a plain IntegerField from Value(3) combined with an AutoField column) — resolves to an IntegerField output instead of raising a 'mixed output-field types' FieldError.

When rendering a blocktranslate/blocktrans tag that carries a plural count (i.e. a `count` option that provides both a counter variable and counter expression), if the value that the counter expression resolves to in the render context is not one of the numeric types Decimal, float, or int (e.g. it is a str, list, None, or other non-numeric type), render() raises a TemplateSyntaxError rather than proceeding to plural-form selection and '%'-formatting. The raised error's message is "%r argument to %r tag must be a number." where the first %r is the counter variable name and the second is the tag name (blocktranslate/blocktrans).

Calling QuerySet.bulk_create() with an object whose concrete ForeignKey/OneToOne relation is cached (assigned) to an object that has no pk (obj.pk is None) raises a ValueError with message "bulk_create() prohibited to prevent data loss due to unsaved related object '<field name>'." instead of inserting the row.

When makemessages processes files whose translations cannot be assigned to a locale path (locale_dir is NO_LOCALE_DIR) but messages were produced, the raised CommandError message is: "Unable to find a locale path to store translations for file <normpath-of-first-build-file>. Make sure the 'locale' directory exist in an app or LOCALE_PATHS setting is set." (precisely, the message equals the concatenation given, i.e. there is a file path after 'file ' and the sentence is followed by the hint text).

When a positional (non-keyword) argument passed to call_command (an element of the *args sequence) is a list or tuple, each element of that collection is stringified with str() and treated as a separate token in the simulated argument parse, so that a collection supplied for an nargs-style positional resolves to its individual parsed values rather than one token holding the whole collection's str() representation.

URLPattern.check() reports a system-check Error with id 'urls.E009' when the pattern's callback is a class (not an instance) that subclasses django.views.View, whose message describes the pattern and advises passing {ViewName}.as_view() instead of the class itself.
In get_connection_params, when settings NAME is None, the returned connection params set database to 'postgres' and do not forward any 'service' OPTIONS entry to psycopg2.

ExceptionReporter.html_template_path and text_template_path yield the paths of the builtin technical_500.html and technical_500.txt templates (resolved lazily via builtin_template_path) rather than via a module-level constant; technical_404_response and default_urlconf read technical_404.html and default_urlconf.html from the same lazily-derived builtin template directory.

When a concrete (DB column-bearing) Field is contributed to a model class, the field's attribute access (descriptor) is always installed on that model class regardless of whether the same-named attribute is already present on or inherited by the model, so the field's attribute takes precedence over (shadows) any pre-existing colliding class-level attribute (method, classmethod, or property/data-descriptor inherited from a base, e.g. an abstract model).

When CursorDebugWrapper.debug_sql emits a query-log entry to the 'django.db.backends' logger, the rendered debug message text appends the database connection's alias to the existing '(duration) sql; args=params' format, i.e. the message ends with '; alias=' followed by the connection alias (self.db.alias) after the args component.

QuerySet.iterator() called on a QuerySet that currently has prefetch_related() lookups set, with chunk_size omitted (None, the new default), emits a DeprecationWarning whose message starts 'Using QuerySet.iterator() after prefetch_related() without specifying chunk_size is deprecated.', and does not raise an exception.

Command.username_is_unique (a cached_property) returns True when the username field has unique=True OR some entry in UserModel._meta.total_unique_constraints has exactly one field equal to the username field's name (i.e., a single-field UniqueConstraint declaring the username field); otherwise it returns False. (A multi-field constraint that includes the username field does not make it return True.)

Invoking the length_is template filter now emits, on every call, a deprecation warning of category RemovedInDjango51Warning with the message 'The length_is template filter is deprecated in favor of the length template filter and the == operator within an {% if %} tag.' (the warning is issued unconditionally, before any length/int computation and independent of the value/arg or the returned result).

For an on_delete handler carrying the lazy marker (SET_NULL, SET_DEFAULT, or SET), the handler is invoked during collection even when its related-rows queryset would evaluate to empty; previously such handlers were only invoked when the related queryset was already non-empty/realized.

BaseFormSet.empty_form returns a form instance (rather than raising a TypeError about receiving multiple values for the same keyword argument) when the formset was constructed with form_kwargs whose keys overlap the reserved empty-form keyword arguments empty_permitted, auto_id, prefix, use_required_attribute, and/or renderer.

When validating a Decimal whose value is zero expressed with a non-negative exponent (significand tuple (0,) and exponent >= 0, e.g. Decimal('0E+1') or Decimal('0E+2')), DecimalValidator counts it as a single digit (1), not as len(digit_tuple) + exponent digits.

QuerySet.aupdate_or_create accepts an additional keyword parameter create_defaults and forwards it (together with defaults) to update_or_create, so its observable behavior matches update_or_create when awaited.

When bind_template raises the informative TypeError described above (after a context processor's result caused a TypeError during merging), the newly raised TypeError carries the original TypeError as its chained cause (__cause__), so both exceptions remain visible to the caller.

Figure(...) construction raises ValueError (with a message stating the size must be positive finite) when the figsize argument has any dimension that is non-finite or not strictly positive (i.e. zero or negative), so a figure whose width or height is 0 or negative is never successfully constructed.

Calling selector.set_handle_props(**handle_props) applies the given properties to each of the selector's handle/vertex artists (e.g. RectangleSelector corner/edge/center markers, SpanSelector edge handles, PolygonSelector vertex handles), so their rendered appearance is updated immediately; the props are also recorded in _handle_props for future handles.

After applying a value range, the RangeSlider's filled selection polygon self.poly is (re)positioned to span from the low endpoint to the high endpoint along the slider's value axis while covering only the mid-width band (0.25 to 0.75) across the perpendicular track direction: for orientation "vertical" the fill spans the vertical data range across the horizontal .25–.75 band, and for "horizontal" it spans the horizontal data range across the vertical .25–.75 band.

After pyplot.switch_backend() completes a switch to a concrete (named, non-auto-sentinel) backend, the current shell's REPL/pylab display hook is (re)installed: in an interactive matplotlib session -- including an IPython '--pylab' session where install_repl_displayhook registers pyplot._draw_all_if_interactive as the IPython post_execute handler -- figures are automatically re-drawn at the end of subsequent input commands (interactive auto-redraw is active). This holds whether the backend load is the session's first lazy load through _get_backend_mod or a later explicit backend switch reached through any other entry point; previously the hook was installed only inside _get_backend_mod's `if _backend_mod is None` first-lazy-load branch, so a backend switch performed once a backend was already loaded (e.g. via an explicit switch_backend / matplotlib.use call) left the auto-redraw display hook unregistered.

Reading `_cachedRenderer` on a `SubFigure` does not raise AttributeError (even when the SubFigure has not yet been drawn, in which case previously the attribute was undefined on the instance) and returns the `_cachedRenderer` value of the SubFigure's parent figure (`SubFigure._parent`).

A constructed Legend instance exposes a public instance attribute `legend_handles` whose value is the list of Artist objects actually added as legend-handle entries (one per retained legend entry, in the same order and aligned with `legend.texts`); the list is reassigned at the end of `_init_legend_box` to the finalized `handle_list`, and it is precisely the list that `get_lines`, `get_patches`, and the labelcolor color-getter loop read from.

In the mesh-data setup shared by pcolor/pcolormesh (Axes._pcolorargs), the number of rows and columns of the mesh is derived from the first two dimensions of C only, so C with more than two dimensions (notably 3D RGB(A) image data of shape (M,N,3) or (M,N,4)) is accepted rather than raising an unpacking error; the mesh is laid out on an M×N grid of the leading dims.

Axes3D.plot builds its data line through _get_lines._plot_args passing the invoking 3D Axes itself, so unit processing/axis update from plotted (unit-bearing, e.g. y) data applies to the 3D axes the plot was called on even when that axes' _get_lines handler originated elsewhere.

AnnotationBbox.get_tightbbox can be called without an explicit renderer (renderer=None); it then uses the owning Figure's default renderer, so that placement update and child tightbbox queries are performed against a valid renderer.

Calling Axis.set_ticks(ticks) (with labels=None and minor not given) while passing one or more extra keyword-only styling/Text arguments (i.e. kwargs is non-empty) raises a ValueError whose message states 'Incorrect use of keyword argument' followed by the repr of the first such keyword argument passed, and goes on to say that keyword arguments other than 'minor' modify the text labels and can only be used if 'labels' are passed as well.

seaborn.external.version.Version parses a PEP-440 version string (with optional epoch, pre/post/dev/local segments); constructing it from an invalid version string raises InvalidVersion (a ValueError subclass), and its ordering comparisons follow PEP 440 normalization so that e.g. '3.0' and '3.0.0' compare equal and pre/post/dev/local orderings are respected.

When a scatter-plot is drawn with a point-estimate aggregation (i.e. x_estimator or x_bins is in effect, so per-x estimate points plus vertical confidence-interval bars are rendered) and an alpha value is supplied in the scatter keywords (e.g. via regplot/lmplot scatter_kws), the vertical confidence-interval error-bar lines drawn at each estimate point are rendered with that same alpha rather than with their previous full-opacity default.

HTTPAdapter.send no longer eagerly reads the response body (`.content`) for a non-stream request (stream=False); it builds and returns the Response without having preloaded/decode-read the content, so a Content-Encoding or chunked decoding failure of the raw response is not raised by send itself (the response body is left for the caller/another layer to consume).

Request.register_hook continues to store a hook value that is not a list, tuple, or set (e.g. a single callable) as a single entry appended to self.hooks[event], preserving single-hook registration semantics.
When max_gap is provided and is not a scalar (e.g. any array-like or list), interpolate_na raises ValueError with message 'max_gap must be a scalar.'

When xarray.combine_by_coords is called with fill_value=None, each group of datasets (after being ordered from dimension coordinates) must create a complete hypercube; if datasets are missing such that the group does not form a complete hypercube, combine_by_coords raises a ValueError instead of returning a Dataset with missing/filled values.

When _config_initialization finds unrecognized command-line options still left in the parsed argument list (entries beginning with '-' or '--'), it no longer raises _UnrecognizedOptionError (and hence no longer causes an uncaught exception traceback); instead it delegates to the linter's argument parser error handling (linter._arg_parser.error), which presents the parser's usage/error message on stderr and terminates execution (argparse's exit-code-2 behavior under its default settings) rather than propagating an exception.

When warn_explicit_for's internal warnings.warn_explicit call raises a Warning (i.e. the warning has been escalated to an error, e.g. via -Werror or warnings-as-errors), warn_explicit_for re-raises an exception of the SAME type as the raised Warning whose message string is the original warning message followed by the offending method's location, "\n at <filename>:<lineno>", where <filename> is inspect.getfile(method) and <lineno> is method.__code__.co_firstlineno.

Assertion rewriting now gives assignment expressions (the walrus operator `:=`, ast.NamedExpr on Python >= 3.8) a dedicated visitor: a walrus that is part of a rewritten assertion's test is turned into an assignment that is snapshotted and described in the assertion's introspection, so a failing assertion whose condition contains a walrus produces an explanation that references the walrus's bound value/name like an ordinary variable, instead of the walrus falling through to generic handling that rewrites/mis-renders it.

on_rm_rf_error now accepts the calling convention used by shutil.rmtree(onexc=...), where its exception argument ('exc') is a bare BaseException instance, in addition to the legacy (type, exception, traceback) exc-info triple; under the bare-instance convention it discriminates errors with outcomes matching those for the triple form: a FileNotFoundError causes it to return False without warning, any other non-PermissionError exception causes it to emit a PytestWarning and return False, and a PermissionError reaching the deletion handling (chmod-and-retry vs. 'unknown function' warning) behaves as before.

Calling pytest.raises(expected_exception) with a falsy expected_exception (e.g. the empty tuple ()) immediately raises ValueError, raised by the raises() call itself before any code block runs or a context manager is returned, rather than deferring a less clear failure to context-exit or validation.

get_feature_names raises a ValueError with message of form "input_features should have length equal to number of features ({n_features}), got {given_length}" when a supplied input_features has length differing from the number of input features (len(self.categories_)).

_load_imgs (the JPEG-decoding step behind fetch_lfw_people and fetch_lfw_pairs) decodes each face JPEG and, when resize is not None, resizes it using sklearn/externals/_pilutil's imread and imresize, i.e. PIL/pillow-driven helpers rather than lazily imported scipy.misc.imread/imresize, so that face decoding requires only that Pillow be installed and no longer depends on scipy.misc and no scipy.misc DeprecationWarning is emitted.

In check_methods_subset_invariance, comparing a method's whole-set result with its per-sample results handles tuple-valued method outputs (e.g. some score_samples forms): only the first element of the returned tuple is used in the comparison, for both the whole-set call and each single-sample call.

The default value of the TfidfVectorizer.dtype parameter is np.float64 (rather than the integer np.int64 dtype inherited from CountVectorizer), so a TfidfVectorizer constructed without an explicit dtype stores dtype=np.float64.

TfidfVectorizer.idf_ is writable: assigning an iterable of IDF weights to vectorizer.idf_ propagates them to the inner TfidfTransformer so that they become readable via vectorizer.idf_ and are used for weighting in transform(), overriding the need for them to be learned by fit().
FunctionTransformer's __init__ validate parameter defaults to None rather than True: an instance created without passing an explicit validate value has its validate attribute set to None.

Calling fit on an IsolationForest whose contamination == 'legacy' emits a FutureWarning stating that the default contamination value 0.1 will change to 'auto' in version 0.22 and that this will change the predict method behavior.

When GridSearchCV/RandomizedSearchCV.fit schedules fits over the product of the candidate params and the CV split iterator but zero individual fits are actually produced (e.g. the CV iterator yields no splits, or there are no candidates), fit raises a ValueError whose message reports that no fits were performed rather than proceeding to accumulate/format an empty result set.

When analyzer is a callable and input is 'file' or 'filename', calling build_analyzer triggers a one-time validation probe in which the callable analyzer is invoked on the string name of a file that does not exist; if that invocation raises FileNotFoundError, or raises AttributeError with message "'str' object has no attribute 'read'", a warning classified as ChangedBehaviorWarning whose message begins 'Since v0.21, vectorizers pass the data to the custom analyzer...' is emitted; for any other outcome (the callable returns successfully or raises some other exception) no such ChangedBehaviorWarning is emitted and the exception is swallowed without propagating.

When a scalar Number `sample_weight` (with `sample_weight is not None`) is passed to BaseDecisionTree.fit, fit no longer raises; instead the estimator fits with that constant weight applied equally to every sample (i.e. equivalent to equal weighting).

For any normalization mode, divisions that would otherwise yield NaN (arising from a zero row, zero column, or zero total sum) are replaced with 0 in the returned confusion_matrix, rather than being surfaced as NaN/Inf entries (division operations are carried out with runtime floating-point errors suppressed).

_get_n_samples_bootstrap, when given a float (Real) max_samples, returns a count of round(n_samples * max_samples) that is never below 1: if round(n_samples * max_samples) would be 0, the returned number of bootstrap samples is 1.

When PowerTransformer fits with method='box-cox' on data that contains a column (feature) consisting entirely of NaN values, the fit/fit_transform raises a ValueError (rather than attempting to compute the Box-Cox lambda on an empty non-NaN slice and failing with an unpacking error).

The hardcoded-extlink-detector external link checker does not emit its 'could be replaced by an extlink' replacement-suggestion warning when the captured value (the portion of the URI matching the extlink base pattern's %s capture) contains a forward slash '/', even if the URI otherwise matches an extlink base pattern with a non-empty value.

When rendering a `footnote` node that is tagged `referred` (i.e. it is referenced more than once, so the later references have been rewritten to `footnotemark` nodes by the LaTeXFootnoteTransform), the emitted LaTeX is a plain footnote environment that starts directly with `\begin{footnote}[<label>]\sphinxAtStartFootnote`, and the writer no longer prefixes that environment with a `\sphinxstepexplicit ` invocation and no longer inserts a `\phantomsection\label{\thesphinxscope.<label>}%` anchor (with its trailing comment-newline) inside the environment body.

Description-typehints mode is driven by the autodoc_typehints config value staying equal to 'description' during the build (it is no longer internally rewritten to 'none' by a config-inited handler); description rendering no longer depends on any separately set runtime flag.

In GoogleDocstring/NumpyDocstring._parse_methods_section, when the docstring was processed with options that contain the 'noindex' key (i.e. the enclosing auto directive carried :noindex:), each generated '.. method:: <name>' line is immediately followed by an indented ':noindex:' option line (inserted before the description content and trailing blank line), so the emitted method directive carries :noindex:.

When autodoc_typehints == 'description' and a py object's contentnode is being transformed, if the contentnode's parent desc_signature node lacks the required context attributes (a missing 'module' and/or 'fullname', raising KeyError on attribute access), sphinx.ext.autodoc.typehints.merge_typehints must not propagate the KeyError to abort the build; instead it must cleanly return without modifying the contentnode or injecting any type-hint fields.

IndexEntries.create_index orders the top-level entries so that every symbol entry (an entry whose NFD-normalized, lowercased key with any leading right-to-left mark stripped does not begin with an alphabetic character or '_', e.g. entries starting with '£', '←', '&', or '@') sorts before every entry beginning with an alphabetic character or '_', regardless of the symbol's Unicode code point; consequently the returned grouped index contains its symbol entries in a single contiguous symbol group (keyed _('Symbols')) that appears first, before the alphabetical groups, instead of allowing non-ASCII symbols to sort after the letter entries and thereby emit a second, non-adjacent Symbols section.

The viewcode extension no longer inserts pending_xref nodes of reftype 'viewcode' into the doctree; nevertheless, any such pending_xref still reaching the missing_reference handler is resolved into a source reference link as before, and resolving one of these legacy nodes emits a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning.

Autosummary's internal documenter works with classes without error even though its synthetic app/config is built outside normal application setup, because the synthetic config used there also declares `autodoc_class_signature` with the same default value ('mixed').

restify(cls) returns a string argument unchanged (verbatim), so when cls is an instance of str the return value equals the input string itself; previously such an argument was not matched by the class-handling branches and resulted in its repr() (quoted form) being returned.

Arguments passed to _print_Or that bind less tightly than Or (e.g. nested conjunction operands) are wrapped in parentheses so disjunctions of conjunctions print e.g. '(x & ~y) | (y & ~x)' and disjunctions over multiple relationals print each <relational>-conjunction in parentheses, preserving the disjunction's operands as distinct grouped terms.

When the first argument is a Poly with exactly one generator and k is a positive Integer (with x finite and not +/-oo), RisingFactorial.eval returns the expanded functional product of the shifted polynomial, i.e. x(y)*x(y+1)*...*x(y+k-1) as a Poly (e.g. rf(Poly(x**3, x), 2) -> Poly(x**6 + 3*x**5 + 3*x**4 + x**3, x, domain='ZZ')).

For a Function instance with a non-empty argument list, __new__ performs the automatic numeric evalf exactly when evaluate is enabled, the constructed object is an instance of the class, and every argument is one that should be auto-evalf'd (all return positive _should_evalf precision); in that case it returns the result numerically evaluated to a number of decimal places derived from the maximum argument precision. When evaluate is disabled, the object is not an instance of the class, or the instance has no arguments, no auto-evaluation occurs and the constructed result is returned as-is.

For an Add or Mul instance whose `as_independent(Symbol, AppliedUndef)` yields a non-identity numeric part x and a non-trivial tail (the "pure number" path of AssocOp._eval_evalf), `_eval_evalf(prec)` returns the freshly-constructed flat expression `self.func(x, e1, e2, ...)` where each `ei` is the individual result of that tail argument's own `_eval_evalf(prec)` (the original tail argument kept when its `_eval_evalf` returns None); this reconstruction is performed unconditionally on every call, rather than only when the per-tail-argument evaluations actually changed something.
Modulo (Mod or %) with a divisor that is exactly zero raises ZeroDivisionError rather than attempting to evaluate the remainder.

ConditionSet's third argument base_set is optional, defaulting to S.UniversalSet, so ConditionSet(sym, condition) (with no base set) constructs a ConditionSet whose .base_set is S.UniversalSet instead of raising a TypeError.

CodePrinter._print_Function treats an applied Function whose name is not among the printer's known_functions and which has no inlined `_imp_` Lambda conditionally: when it satisfies expr.is_Function and the printer's `allow_unknown_functions` setting is truthy, it is emitted as a literal call of the form `<printed func>(<printed arg1>, <printed arg2>, …)` (the function name and each argument printed recursively, comma-joined with ', ') instead of being routed to _print_not_supported; when `allow_unknown_functions` is False (or expr.is_Function is false) such a Function is still recorded as Not supported and returned via the pre-existing fallback.

FCodePrinter (e.g. via fcode) raises NotImplementedError when asked to print a SymPy Mod / % expression while the 'standard' setting is 66 or 77 (the raised message states that Python's % operator and SymPy's Mod() are not supported by Fortran 66 or 77); since the default 'standard' is 77, a plain fcode(Mod(...)) now raises.
srepr(S.Integers) (ReprPrinter._print_Integers) returns the string 'Integers' rather than the emptyPrinter fallback 'Integers()'.

LatexPrinter now prints a HadamardPower (elementwise matrix power) matrix expression instead of falling through to a generic constructor-style print: the base is printed with the standard power-handling used for ordinary x**n superscripts and the exponent is shown as an elementwise (ring)∘ marker, yielding output of the form `{base}^{\circ {<exp>}}` (e.g. a bare MatrixSymbol base printed as `A^{\circ {2}}`).
calling isqrt with a negative argument raises ValueError (with message 'n must be nonnegative') rather than computing via the float/integer-nthroot path
Contains(x, s).as_set() raises NotImplementedError instead of returning the Contains object itself.

In the dict returned by sympy.logic.boolalg._finger, the fifth element of each symbol's fingerprint tuple is a sorted tuple of integer triples (i, j, k), where i is the number of arguments of an And- or Or-function appearing among the top-level arguments in which that symbol occurs as a non-negated Symbol literal, j is the number of that function's arguments that are Not(literal), and k is the number of such functions (sharing the same (i, j)) in which the symbol so occurs; a symbol that never occurs as a non-negated Symbol literal inside any And/Or top-level argument (e.g. it only occurs as a bare top-level symbol, as in x&~y, or only inside Not(·)) receives an empty tuple ( ) as its fifth element.

A new physical constant named `elementary_charge`, with symbol/abbreviation "e", of electric-charge dimension (`charge`), and numeric scale factor `1.602176634e-19 * coulomb`, is defined and exported from the `sympy.physics.units` namespace (accessible as `u.elementary_charge`).

When IndexedBase is constructed from a string label together with assumptions passed as keyword arguments, the Symbol stored as the resulting label (args[0] / label property) is created with exactly those assumptions, so the label itself carries the assumption set (e.g. IndexedBase('A', real=True).label.is_real is True and the label is the Symbol 'A' with the real assumption).

Under evaluation-disabled context (evaluate(False)), adding (or the reflected add of) oo or -oo with any Number operand no longer collapses to the eager infinite/NaN result (nan/oo/-oo); instead it produces an unevaluated Add expression (e.g. Add(oo, -1) rather than oo).

For such an integer-ImageSet vs. Integers/imageSet intersection, when f(n)=g(m) admits exactly one parametric (infinite) solution family for n with a single free symbol, the intersection is returned as the ImageSet { f(h(t)) : t in Integers } with the resulting lambda expression expanded.
SchurNumber(S.Infinity) evaluates (via eval) to S.Infinity.

When uniq iterates over a seq whose length is determinable at call time (len(seq) succeeds and is recorded), if the seq is subsequently mutated during iteration so that its current length no longer equals the length recorded when uniq was called, iteration raises RuntimeError (whose message contains 'sequence changed size during iteration') instead of silently continuing with corrupted output; this detection applies on the normal hashable-element dedup path and on the unhashable-element (TypeError) fallback path.

Range.is_finite_set evaluates to True for a Range whose start and stop are both known integers (covering concrete integer bounds and integer-valued symbolic bounds), i.e. every bounded integer range is reported finite regardless of its step or size.

When a MatMul consists of two factors, one being a MatAdd matrix expression and the other a Rational scalar, canonicalization (MatMul.doit/canonicalize) now distributes the scalar over the MatAdd rather than leaving the scalar-times-sum as an unevaluated product. That is, the product of the Rational `r` with the MatAdd of terms, written in either factor order (scalar before the sum or after the sum), evaluates to a MatAdd of the scalar applied to each term individually; e.g. `r*(A+B)` (and the reversed-order form) evaluates to `r*A + r*B`, each `r*term` result itself being passed through doit.

When the domain of a DDM is a RealField (RR) or ComplexField (CC), DDM.rref selects each pivot by row-pivoting within the column: among the not-yet-processed rows it chooses the one whose entry has the largest absolute value, using that row as the pivot row before continuing with the standard elimination; matrices over these inexact fields are therefore reduced correctly and the returned reduced-row-echelon form and pivot list match a properly row-pivoted RREF rather than picking an accidentally small leading entry as the pivot.
LaTeX printing of a single-argument LambertW raised to a power produces the exponent as a superscript attached to the W symbol: W^{n}\left(z\right) where n is the printed exponent.

Mul.is_integer reports False (not None/undecidable) for products where the remaining (post-±1-removal) numerator factors are all odd while at least one denominator factor is even, and for forms having a single even numerator Integer whose combined factor-of-2 content from the even denominators strictly exceeds the numerator's own factor-of-2 count.

For f an instance of Min or Max containing the decomposition symbol, when every symbol-containing argument of f has a decompogen whose trailing elements (all elements after the first, after an argument that itself yields exactly one decomposition element is treated as if it decomposed as [symbol, arg]) are mutually identical, decompogen(f, symbol) returns [Min_or_Max_same_type] + [that common trailing sequence], where the rebuilt Min/Max preserves the same type (Min stays Min, Max stays Max) and the same positions/values of symbol-free arguments, with each symbol-containing argument position replaced by the first element of that argument's own decompogen.

MathematicaParser._from_mathematica_to_tokens tokenizes a comment-cleaned code split with the tokenizer regex (tokenizer.findall) only when that split is a str and is all-ASCII; a str split containing any non-ASCII character (e.g. a Greek letter such as λ) is instead appended to the returned token list as a single opaque token equal to the whole split, so the non-ASCII characters are preserved rather than silently dropped by findall. (Equivalently, the two cases that previously took the tokenizer route — a plain ASCII split and a non-ASCII split — now differ: the latter is not fragmented.)
Multiplying two Prefixes whose scale factors are reciprocal (scale product == 1) yields S.One (a SymPy Integer equal to 1) rather than the bare Python integer 1, e.g. m*k == 1 still holds.

The ITRS frame carries an EarthLocation 'location' frame attribute whose default is the centre of the Earth, so an ITRS frame/coordinate can be created (or defaulted) with either an explicit topocentric (non-geocentric) observing site or, by default, the geocenter, and it can be transformed to a topocentric ITRS that is offset from the geocenter.

When Quantity.__array_ufunc__ raises a TypeError or ValueError while handling a numpy ufunc and every one of the inputs and out arguments has a __array_ufunc__ that is only None, np.ndarray.__array_ufunc__, or Quantity.__array_ufunc__ (i.e., no genuinely custom override), the original exception is re-raised/propagated to the caller unchanged rather than being swallowed or converted to NotImplemented.

_line_type recognizes the missing-value token 'NO' and the 'nan' data token case-insensitively during line classification: a row consisting of multiple NO tokens in any letter case (e.g. 'no no no no') is still classified as 'new' (a table separator), and a data row whose values include NO/nan in mixed or lowercase casing (e.g. '1.2 no' or 'NAN') is classified as a data line of the correct column count rather than rejected as unrecognized.

Header.fromstring accepts a `bytes` first argument (in addition to `str`) and builds a Header whose parsed cards are equivalent to parsing the latin-1 decoding of those bytes; arbitrary byte values (including non-ASCII, which latin-1 always decodes) are accepted without raising a TypeError/UnicodeDecodeError, with bytes passed onward to Card.fromstring for card parsing.

When FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS is left at its default and a FileSystemStorage is constructed without an explicit file_permissions_mode, a file saved through that storage is chmod'd to permission mode 0o644 after being stored (in both the file-move and streamed-write save paths), rather than retaining the source temp-file mode or the umask-derived creation mode.

UUIDField.get_prep_value coerces input through UUIDField.to_python: a non-uuid.UUID string-hexadecimal or integer value is converted into the corresponding uuid.UUID instance (so that a call such as pk.get_prep_value(<string object_id>) yields a uuid.UUID comparable to a UUID primary-key value), an already-uuid.UUID value and None are returned unchanged, and an unparseable value raises the same ValidationError as to_python.

When trimming leading joins off the exclude subquery, a leading 'self'/base-table join may only be removed when the following join is not tied to a FilteredRelation; if that join originates from a FilteredRelation (an INNER join carrying one), it is kept so that the FilteredRelation's filter condition continues to apply inside the subquery.

The '--skip-checks' parser argument is added to a command's parser only when requires_system_checks is True; a command whose requires_system_checks is False does not gain a --skip-checks parser option (so its help output does not list the flag and the parser does not bind it).

Field.get_choices returns a relation's related objects in the related model's default ordering (the ordering of its default manager, i.e. its Meta.ordering) when the 'ordering' argument is empty/() — instead of stripping that default ordering by appending a blank order_by() — and orders them by the supplied non-empty 'ordering' fields when such are given.

replace_unnamed_groups replaces an unnamed capture group that terminates the regex pattern at its very end (its closing ')' is the last character, with no following literal token, including nested groups such as '((x|y)\w+)') with '<var>'. E.g. '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(\w+)' is returned as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>' and '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/((x|y)\w+)' as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>'.

Calling str() on any member of a Choices-derived enum class (Choices itself, IntegerChoices, TextChoices, or a user subclass) returns the string form of that member's value (str(member.value)) rather than the standard enum string form that names the member, e.g. 'MyEnum.MEMBER_NAME' or the enum class reference.

Assigning a value to the pk attribute on a multi-table-inheritance (concrete-parent) model instance, in addition to setting the instance's own local primary-key attribute, also sets the instance attribute for the remote (parent) pk of every parent link registered in _meta.parents whose field is not the model's own primary-key field to that same assigned value. Non-parent-linked, single-table models are unaffected: pk assignment still only sets the local pk attribute.

When alter_index_together removes an index_together grouping (an entry in the old set not present in the new), the schema editor locates for deletion only a constraint whose introspection reports index=True and unique=False for those columns, i.e. a plain (non-unique) index; a unique constraint spanning the very same columns is excluded from the deletion lookup so that it is not deleted and the removal does not fail with a "Found wrong number..." ValueError merely because that unique constraint exists.

The flush management command calls connection.ops.execute_sql_flush with only the sql list (no database-alias argument), so the flush is performed on the connection bound to the --database option's alias.

On a backend with has_native_duration_field False, when both operands of a CombinedExpression resolve to internal type DurationField the expression is not wrapped through DurationExpression/combine_duration_expression; it is compiled by the ordinary branch that compiles each operand and joins them with connection.ops.combine_expression and the raw connector, so it is applied exactly once.

During CombinedExpression.resolve_expression, a combined arithmetic expression whose two operands resolve to different field internal types where at least one is DurationField (a DurationField mixed with a non-duration field) is rewritten, at resolution time, into a DurationExpression and recursively resolved; the rewritten DurationExpression is resolved as a duration-arithmetic expression on every backend rather than only on backends lacking a native duration field.

On backend connections whose JSON support is not native (connection.features.has_native_json_field is False), the rhs values of a key-transform __in lookup are not produced by the stock In rhs preparation alone; instead each candidate value is wrapped by an extraction function so that membership is checked against the decoded JSON key value.

When ordering two Field instances with equal creation_counters: an unattached field (no model) orders before a model-attached field; two fields both attached to models are ordered by comparing their models' (app_label, model_name) tuples; two unattached fields with equal counters are not strictly ordered relative to one another.

On POSIX systems, locks.lock() returns False (does not raise) when the flock call fails with BlockingIOError, i.e. when a non-blocking (LOCK_NB) lock attempt is denied due to contention; exceptions other than BlockingIOError propagate.

OutputWrapper.flush() delegates to the flush() method of the wrapped stream (self._out) when that stream has a flush attribute, and does nothing (neither raising nor forwarding) when it does not — so that calling flush() on an OutputWrapper no longer raises (as the previously inherited io.TextIOBase.flush behavior did) and instead flushes the underlying destination stream.

The email appended to the hashed value is taken from the email field resolved via user.get_email_field_name() (cls.EMAIL_FIELD, defaulting to 'email'), so on a custom user model whose EMAIL_FIELD names a different attribute, it is that attribute's value whose later change invalidates the token.
Files that are not adjustable continue to be yielded immediately during the initial single post-processing pass (their results are not deferred to the end).

BaseDatabaseClient.runshell invokes the client executable via subprocess.run with env=None (so the child inherits the calling process's os.environ) whenever settings_to_cmd_args_env returns a falsy env value such as an empty dict, instead of passing that empty dict/env to the subprocess.

When the search term contains multiple words and search_fields includes a lookup that traverses a relation (e.g. a ForeignKey path), the per-word match criteria are combined into a single conjunction (one queryset.filter call over a single AND of the per-word OR query groups) rather than applying an independent filter per word — so the number of traversals/joins to the related model introduced by a multi-word search does not multiply with the number of words (each related search relation is exercised once for the whole term, not once per word).

When adding a field whose primary_key is True to an existing model on SQLite, DatabaseSchemaEditor.add_field uses the full table-remake procedure (_remake_table, which rebuilds the table) rather than a plain 'ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN', so the new primary-key column/semantics are realized on the rebuilt table rather than attempted via unsupported inline ALTER.

get_template_directories() skips any falsy/empty-string directory returned by a template loader's get_dirs() (it only considers non-empty directories that are not Django paths), so such an entry does not cause Path.cwd() to be added to the returned set of template directories.

When a defer()/only() column spec traverses an intermediate relation whose target model is a proxy model, Query.deferred_to_data registers the required pk/reference fields under the proxy's concrete backing model (so the concrete model's pk column is included among the selected/loaded columns), and the resulting query loads and populates the related (proxy) object with its pk correctly set rather than failing during object population because the pk column is missing.

On any path where floatformat cannot produce a formatted result and echoes the input value back unmodified (i.e. when arg is not a valid integer magnitude, or when the value cannot be processed as a Decimal), a Decimal input is echoed as its plain digit string (str form), e.g. '555.555', rather than as its repr Python-literal form "Decimal('555.555')".

A ModelForm subclass whose Meta class declares a formfield_callback has that callback applied when constructing that form's model-derived fields: each model field is routed through the Meta's callback rather than the default f.formfield() building.

When.as_sql: when the condition compiles to an empty SQL string (a filter that matches every row, e.g. a negated empty lookup like ~Q(pk__in=[])), the CASE WHEN branch is emitted with an always-true predicate as its condition instead of a malformed/empty condition — so the WHEN's THEN result is returned for every row.
The --check option help text states that it exits with a non-zero status when model changes are missing migrations and that it does not actually write the migration files.

get_aggregation decides whether to route the aggregate through the subquery-wrapping path based on whether existing annotations actually involve aggregate/window computation: it uses a subquery only if some existing selected annotation contains an aggregate or an OVER clause, or if some existing filter references an aggregate/window alias (a HAVING/QUALIFY condition); the mere presence of pre-existing annotations that are neither is no longer sufficient to force a subquery.

AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_fallback_hash() is a generator that, for each entry of settings.SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS in order, yields a fallback session-auth-hash computed from the user's password field using that fallback secret as the HMAC secret (i.e., it yields len(settings.SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS) values, each a distinct fallback-secret-derived hash).

In Query.get_aggregation, when any aggregate expression being resolved references an existing annotation whose underlying expression reports contains_over_clause (i.e. a window-function annotation such as one built with django.db.models.Window), the query is routed to the wrapped-subquery aggregation path: the row-level (window) computation is performed in an inner query and the aggregate is applied over its results in the outer query, rather than inlining the window expression directly inside the aggregate in a single SELECT. Observable effect: a QuerySet such as .annotate(<window alias>).aggregate(<Aggregate of that alias>) executes without producing invalid or incorrect SQL and returns a value equal to applying the aggregate to the per-row window values.
Constructing a Legend whose parent is neither an Axes nor a FigureBase raises TypeError with the exact message 'Legend needs either Axes or FigureBase as parent'.

UnitData.update invoked with empty data does not emit the INFO-level log message 'Using categorical units to plot a list of strings that are all parsable as floats or dates...' (the message is suppressed when data is empty even though the all-convertible check is vacuously true).

On exit of the matplotlib.rc_context context manager, rcParams['backend'] is left untouched: whatever backend value (or resolution of the auto-backend sentinel) is in effect at the end of the context body is preserved after the context exits, rather than being restored to its value at context entry. In particular, an auto-backend sentinel present in the global rcParams at context entry is never re-installed into rcParams['backend'] by the context's cleanup, and a backend set or resolved inside the body (e.g. by figure creation, by the supplied fname/rc, or by matplotlib.use) is not rolled back.
When one Text's visual properties are copied into another Text via `update_from`, the destination also copies the source's per-instance antialiased value.

Collection.set_paths(paths) no longer raises NotImplementedError: it records the passed argument as the collection's paths (so that a subsequent call to the inherited get_paths() returns exactly the passed value) and marks the collection stale.

The nominal auto axis-limit set described above is applied with matplotlib autoscaling disabled for that axis (auto=None), so that the displayed bounds covering all categories are final and are not updated by later autoscale calls or further data on the axis.

For continuous scales whose major formatter does not expose the set_useOffset/set_scientific controls (e.g. a formatter type lacking these methods), the legend tick labels are left formatted exactly as before — the offset/scientific suppression is applied only when the formatter actually supports it.

prepend_scheme_if_needed preserves userinfo/authentication credentials embedded in the input URL across scheme prepending: when the URL's auth component (as parsed by urllib3's parse_url) is non-empty, the returned URL's authority (netloc, reconstructed via urlunparse) includes 'auth@' prefixed onto the host[:port] so the credentials are not dropped from the result.

PandasIndexAdapter exposes a new copy(deep=True) method that returns a new PandasIndexAdapter; with deep=True it wraps a deep copy of the underlying pandas index, with deep=False it shares the same underlying index, and in both cases the adapter's stored dtype is preserved on the returned adapter.

Dataset.merge(other) now accepts a xarray.DataArray as `other` by first converting it to a Dataset via other.to_dataset() before delegating to dataset_merge_method; consequently the DataArray's named data variable and coordinates participate in the merge rather than an AttributeError being raised. (For an unnamed DataArray, to_dataset raises ValueError, so Dataset.merge with an unnamed DataArray raises ValueError rather than AttributeError.)

In the same case (data dtype kind 'u' and `_Unsigned` == "false"), if a `_FillValue` is present in the variable's attrs, that fill value is cast as the corresponding same-width signed integer type (e.g., an itemsize-1 fill value of 255 becomes -1).

When Dataset.set_index builds a new (multi-)index that supersedes an existing index, a coordinate variable belonging to the pre-existing (now-dropped) index — provided it is not among the variables being newly indexed and not itself recreated as one of the new index variables — is re-added to the resulting dataset as a regular de-indexed variable (via to_base_variable) instead of being removed from _variables, so no coordinate is silently deleted and referenced-coordinate integrity is preserved.

When PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__ is called on an adapter whose level is set (not None), the returned numpy array is np.asarray(level_values.values, dtype=dtype) where dtype is the requested dtype argument if one was given, or otherwise the adapter's recorded dtype (self.dtype) — so the result has the requested dtype when one is supplied and otherwise preserves the recorded original level-coordinate dtype rather than whatever dtype pandas' get_level_values would otherwise produce (i.e., an int32 level coordinate is not upcast to int64).

pylint.exports a module-level Boolean constant `IS_PYPY` in `pylint.constants` that is True exactly when the running Python implementation is PyPy (as reported by `platform.python_implementation()`), and False otherwise.

The help/usage text for the `--verbose` (`-v`) and `--enable-all-extensions` command-line options renders those flags with no argument value/metavar placeholder token following them (their per-option metavar is the empty string, threaded through the _CallableArgument conversion and add_argument call), instead of the default dest-derived uppercase placeholder.

Calling _is_ignored_file(element, ignore_list, ignore_list_re, ignore_list_paths_re) returns True iff os.path.basename(element) is a member of ignore_list, or os.path.basename(element) matches (re.match) any pattern in ignore_list_re, or the full element path matches any pattern in ignore_list_paths_re; otherwise returns False.

expand_modules._is_ignored_file normalizes the given element path with os.path.normpath before deciding whether it is ignored, so an element whose literal text only matches an ignore-rule once redundant '.'/'..' segments, non-canonical separators, or trailing path separators are resolved is still treated as ignored: after the fix, an element path that does not literally match an ignore-paths regex (ignore_list_paths_re) but whose normalized form does is reported as ignored (previously it was not).
pylint.modify_sys_path() additionally removes the then-current first element of sys.path when the environment variable PYTHONPATH starts with ':' and PYTHONPATH is not exactly ':'+cwd or ':.'.
Given a list or tuple, pylint.utils._check_regexp_csv yields each element exactly as provided, without splitting, stripping, or otherwise transforming the elements.

LogCaptureHandler.clear() empties the handler's list of captured records (the records attribute holds an empty list after the call, having had all previously accumulated records removed) and resets the handler's captured text stream so that its previously formatted output is discarded.

Under `--pdb`, TestCaseFunction.runtest() suppresses the deferred-tearDown mechanism (which postpones the unittest tearDown until pytest teardown and replaces the testcase's tearDown with a no-op) only when the currently running test is not skipped — now treating a class-level `@unittest.skip` (i.e. __unittest_skip__ set on the enclosing test class) as skipped, so that for a skipped whole class the testcase's real tearDown is left intact and runs normally rather than being deferred/replaced.

In cluster_optics_xi, when a min_cluster_size that is not None is given as a fraction in (0, 1], it is rescaled to max(2, int(min_cluster_size * n_samples)) — the fractional product truncated to an integer with a floor of 2 — rather than remaining a float.

When building the diagram's URL map in html_visit_inheritance_diagram from a resolved class reference (a pending_xref child carrying a 'refuri'): an external intersphinx reference (child with 'internal' falsy, i.e. not default/true) is recorded under the key equal to the substring of the refuri that follows its final '#', while an internal refuri-based reference is recorded under the key equal to its 'reftitle'.

A :glob: toctree pattern never adds a std-generated special page (genindex/modindex/search or any docname whose name coincides with a std label key) as a toctree entry/includefile, even when the glob pattern nominally matches that name.

In prepend_prolog, the set of leading content lines classified as the document's docinfo region (the lines after which the rst_prolog is inserted) is determined by matching each line against docutils' genuine field-list field-marker syntax (e.g. `:Field name: value`), rather than by the presence of any `:\w+:` token in the line. Concretely, while scanning from the top of `content`, a line advances `pos` (the prolog insertion index) only if that line is an actual field-marker entry; a heading or body line that merely contains an inline interpreted-text role form such as `:mod:\`title\`` inside its text is NOT treated as docinfo, so the prolog is inserted before it rather than after its role token.

When Sphinx parses a type annotation into cross-reference nodes (via sphinx.domains.python._parse_annotation, reached from both signature parameter annotations via _parse_arglist and return annotations via handle_signature), any bare-name text equal to the literal string 'None' is turned into a pending_xref node with refdomain='py', reftarget='None', and reftype='obj', so that 'None' is referenced as a Python object/data rather than as a class.

DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature recognizes an object's docstring signature when it is not located on the very first line of the object's docstring text: it scans the lines of each docstring block (skipping non-signature and empty lines) until it finds a signature whose base name matches the documented object, and treats the first such match as the signature.

signature_from_str does not misattribute a default declared on an earlier positional-only parameter to a following, non-defaulted positional-or-keyword parameter: in a signature such as '(a, b=0, /, c)', parameter b keeps default 0 while parameter c in the returned Signature has Parameter.empty as its default (a posonly default must not shift the defaults alignment so that the trailing regular parameter inherits it).

In _skip_member, when a class or exception member whose __qualname__ owner part is a single name (dot-free cls_path) that resolves through the equivalent of a functools.wraps wrapper, the owner-class is looked up in the module globals of the original unwrapped member object rather than the wrapper. Concretely observable: _skip_member returns False (does not skip) for such a functools.wraps-decorated __init__ that has a docstring and is owned by a single-segment class name when napoleon_include_init_with_doc is enabled — i.e. owner detection no longer fails merely because the wrapper's own __globals__ lacks the class name, so the init-with-doc inclusion decision is applied consistently with an undecorated __init__.

When linkcheck checks a URL with a fragment anchor (anchor present, not ignored, and linkcheck_anchors enabled) and the streamed GET of the anchor's base URL (req_url) returns an HTTP error status, the URL is reported based on that HTTP error via the standard status handling (401 as 'working'/'- unauthorized', 503 as 'ignored' with the error, any other error status as 'broken' with the error) rather than being reported as 'Anchor ... not found' after scanning the error document body.

sphinx.ext.autodoc.importer.get_class_members is no longer called with a ModuleAnalyzer argument; its signature has dropped the trailing 'analyzer' parameter so it now takes exactly (subject, objpath, attrgetter).

In DocFieldTransformer.transform, when an otherwise-unknown/argument-mismatched typed field is still re-linked from its single-node text content, the resulting xref is now generated with the document's BuildEnvironment passed through, so that this fallback path applies the same domain field-xref processing and scope (py:module/py:class) as the standard doc-field xref path instead of producing an env-less xref.

ModuleDocumenter.get_object_members(want_all=True) distinguishes between a module whose __all__ is absent (self.__all__ is None) and a module whose __all__ is defined but empty (a list/tuple []); the defined-but-empty case is no longer treated as if __all__ were absent. Consequently, for a module with an empty defined __all__, all module members that are not named in __all__ are marked skipped (member.skipped = True) so none of them get documented, instead of falling into the 'no __all__' branch that returns all members with module-attribute checking enabled.

The Literal-special handling applies only when the rendered base token of the bracketed subscript is exactly the bare name 'Literal' or the dotted 'typing.Literal'; for any other subscript base, value-argument text inside the brackets continues to be handled as ordinary type text (converted to type cross-reference nodes when non-whitespace, as before the patch).

Binary arithmetic that combines a Poly instance with a non-Poly SymPy Expr operand (e.g. a generator Symbol such as x, or a SymPy number such as S(-2)) is dispatched through the Poly's operator methods and yields a Poly-typed result rather than remaining an unevaluated commutative core Mul/Add. In particular x*Poly(x) evaluates to Poly(x**2, x, domain='ZZ') and S(-2)*Poly(x) evaluates to Poly(-2*x, x, domain='ZZ').

When tensor_product_simp is applied to a Mul whose sole non-commutative factor is a Pow whose base is a TensorProduct (possibly multiplied by commutative scalars), it returns the scalar multiplier times a TensorProduct in which the exponent is distributed into each argument, instead of returning the Mul unchanged.

Printing a Lambda object now renders its body expression (both in the single-bound-variable form 'Lambda(<v>, <body>)' and the multi-variable form 'Lambda((...), <body>)') through the printer, so symbols in the body (e.g. under python(...)) are collected and declared, whereas previously only multi-variable argument lists were printed via _print and the body was raw-formatted.

MpmathPrinter renders the integer numerator e.p and denominator e.q of a Rational directly into the emitted code (interpolated verbatim, including the sign of a negative numerator such as Rational(-3,2) being rendered as mpmath.mpf(-3)/mpmath.mpf(2)), so rational values of arbitrary size and either sign are represented losslessly in the generated expression rather than approximated or pre-evaluated at print/parse time.

Printing an unevaluated Min expression (an object whose top-level func is Min, with more than one argument that Min does not collapse to a single symbol/numeral) via mathematica_code / MCodePrinter yields Mathematica function-call bracket notation of the form 'Min[arg1, arg2, ...]' rather than the parenthesized python-call form 'Min(arg1, arg2, ...)' that CodePrinter's fallback dispatch produces.

For a symbol in MathMLPresentationPrinter._print_Symbol whose name decomposes into a base identifier plus subscript(s) and/or superscript(s) (e.g. Symbol('x2') -> base 'x', subscript '2'), the printed top-level element for that symbol is the structural element itself (an <msub> when only a subscript is present, an <msup> when only a superscript is present, or an <msubsup> when both are present), containing the base <mi> and the script content -- the structural element is no longer nested inside an outer <mi> wrapper.

When posify replaces a free symbol whose positivity is unknown with a positive dummy, the dummy carries over all of that symbol's other explicit assumptions (not only positive=True); consequently, querying the returned expression's replacement symbol for any of the original symbol's explicit assumptions (e.g., finite) yields the same truth value as on the original symbol, and likewise for other declared assumptions such as integer/rational/odd/even.

The LaTeX rendering of a Subs expression always encloses the substituted expression (the LaTeX of subs.args[0], the expr being evaluated) in literal \left( ... \right) delimiters, so the emitted form is `\left. \left(<expr>\right) \right|_{\substack{ ... }}` regardless of what expr is.

String is now a subclass of sympy.core.expr.Atom (in addition to Token), so every String instance (and its subclasses QuotedString and Comment) is an instance of Atom and exhibits SymPy atomic semantics (e.g. treated as an atom rather than a container by Basic traversal operations).

When checking a candidate homomorphism whose domain is a PermutationGroup, a presentation relator word containing terms with negative powers (inverses of generators) is evaluated and contributes toward the identity check: each relator term's free-generator symbol maps to the corresponding domain generator and is raised to that term's (possibly negative) power in the accumulated image, so such relators are no longer skipped.
